title: Amazoness Aggro
description:
Eleven Amazoness monsters and three Amazoness Village support an offense that replaces destroyed monsters. Amazoness Swords Woman turns unfavorable battles into damage to the opponent, while Amazoness Paladin and Amazoness Tiger benefit from having allies on the field.

NeoGoat Pro 0.3.2 beta.60 default deck | October 2026

PLAY GUIDE
Establish Village, trade monsters without losing field presence, and save removal for threats that prevent you from battling.

Game Plan
- Search for Amazoness Village with Terraforming and keep a second copy as a replacement; keeping the Field Spell active matters more than putting every Amazoness on the field.
- Use the three Amazoness Paladin to apply pressure and the three Amazoness Swords Woman to punish large monsters. Village only replaces a monster once per turn.
- Use Book of Moon and removal to open up specific battles. Keep resources in hand against Torrential Tribute or Mirror Force.

Opening Turns
- With Village and an Amazoness, activate the Field Spell before committing the monster, and hold interaction so the opponent cannot easily remove both.
- Without Village, Giant Rat or Warrior Lady of the Wasteland can set up your next monster. Reinforcement of the Army can find Swords Woman or Exiled Force depending on the field.

Key Plays and Synergies
- Warrior Lady of the Wasteland recruits an EARTH Warrior with 1500 ATK or less: Swords Woman and Exiled Force are options. Giant Rat can also access Amazoness Tiger.
- After an Amazoness is destroyed and reaches the GY, Village summons another of an equal or lower Level. A destroyed Swords Woman can leave the next one ready.
- Amazoness Spellcaster swaps original ATK to overcome a boss monster. Amazoness Archers reduces ATK by 500 and forces the affected monsters to attack if able.
- Amazoness Archer can Tribute two monsters to deal 1200 damage. Count that finishing option once the opponent is within range, after making any useful attacks.

Common Mistakes
- Tiger is a Beast, and you can only control one. Warrior Lady of the Wasteland and Reinforcement of the Army cannot search for it.
- Village requires destruction and a trip to the GY; banishing, returning a monster, or Tributing it does not trigger the replacement.
- Do not declare Warrior with Tribe-Infecting Virus without counting your own Amazoness. Heavy Storm also destroys Village.
- Amazoness Chain Master costs 1500 LP after being destroyed by battle; use the effect when the information and stolen monster justify the payment.

SIDE DECK GUIDE
Each plan starts from the original deck list and swaps an equal number of cards in and out. Choose a plan based on what you saw in Game 1; do not combine complete plans. These are practice guidelines with verified card counts and legality, not claims of proven performance in human matches.

Side Card Roles
- 2 x Kycoo the Ghost Destroyer: Against Chaos, Gozuki and graveyard-based Fusion decks, it applies pressure and stops the opponent from banishing cards from either graveyard. It does not stop Miracle Fusion or Dragon's Mirror from using only materials on the field. Two copies compensate for the lack of a searcher; the plans replace supporting cards while keeping at least nine Amazoness monsters.
- 2 x Cipher Soldier: Against Warrior and Amazoness decks, it wins battles without filling the deck with removal that feeds Village. As an EARTH Machine with 1350 ATK, it can be summoned by Giant Rat, but not searched by Wasteland or ROTA.
- 2 x Des Wombat: An anti-burn monster that preserves the battle plan and Village. Its 1600 ATK means Giant Rat CANNOT summon it, even though it is an EARTH Beast. Two copies compensate for the lack of a searcher.
- 2 x Seven Tools of the Bandit: Protects important attacks and summons without negating Archers or your own defensive and revival traps. Two copies against traps; each costs 1000 LP and cannot answer the effects of traps that are already active.
- 2 x Dust Tornado: Removes Decree, Skill Drain, Oppression and backrow without touching Village. Two copies handle persistent locks that Seven Tools cannot remove once they have resolved.
- 2 x Spell Shattering Arrow: Destroys opposing Field Spells, Future Fusion and Continuous Spells while preserving your own Village. Bring both copies only against decks with enough face-up Spell targets, not against backrow made entirely of traps.
- 1 x D.D. Warrior: A battle-based answer to a large or recurring boss monster. An EARTH Warrior with 1200 ATK, accessible through ROTA, Rat and Wasteland. This is a single toolbox option, distinct from the LIGHT D.D. Warrior Lady.
- 1 x Nobleman of Crossout: One answer to set defenders and FLIP monsters that requires no battle and does not trigger battle recruiters. It preserves the Amazoness core without adding another Normal Summon.
- 1 x Bottomless Trap Hole: A second copy overall against large Warriors and monsters best dealt with by banishing. One extra copy avoids overloading on traps; it is not an answer to every monster summoned during the Damage Step.

Matchup Side Plans

Warrior / Amazoness mirror
Side In: 2 x Cipher Soldier; 1 x D.D. Warrior; 1 x Bottomless Trap Hole
Side Out: 1 x Tribe-Infecting Virus; 1 x Lightning Vortex; 1 x Amazoness Fighter; 1 x Amazoness Chain Master
4 in, 4 out. Keep nine Amazoness monsters, all three Village and every recruiter. Rat can summon Cipher; ROTA, Rat and Wasteland can access D.D. Warrior. None of those cards makes Cipher a Warrior. Remove Tribe because declaring Warrior would also destroy your own board.

Chaos / Zombie / graveyard decks
Side In: 2 x Kycoo the Ghost Destroyer; 1 x D.D. Warrior
Side Out: 1 x Amazoness Fighter; 1 x Amazoness Chain Master; 1 x Tribe-Infecting Virus
3 in, 3 out. Keep nine Amazoness monsters and every searcher. Kycoo stops the opponent from banishing from graveyards, not from the field or hand. D.D. Warrior removes a boss through battle, but also banishes itself and cannot trigger Village because it is not an Amazoness.

Field Spells, Future Fusion and Continuous Spell engines
Side In: 2 x Spell Shattering Arrow; 2 x Dust Tornado
Side Out: 1 x Amazoness Archers; 1 x Creature Swap; 1 x Smashing Ground; 1 x Amazoness Fighter
4 in, 4 out. Arrow preserves Village while disrupting the opposing engine; Dust handles traps that Arrow cannot touch. Keep Enemy Controller and both Book of Moon as monster interaction.

Burn / stall with Continuous Spells and Traps
Side In: 2 x Des Wombat; 2 x Dust Tornado; 2 x Spell Shattering Arrow; 2 x Seven Tools of the Bandit
Side Out: 1 x Bottomless Trap Hole; 2 x Smashing Ground; 1 x Lightning Vortex; 1 x Mirror Force; 1 x Ring of Destruction; 1 x Exiled Force; 1 x Tribe-Infecting Virus
8 in, 8 out, only after confirming a lock involving both Spells and Traps. Keep the entire Amazoness lineup, Village and its recruiters. Rat cannot summon Wombat; removing Ring and dead defensive cards reduces LP risk. Do not bring in Arrow without enough observed face-up targets.

Counter Traps / set defenders
Side In: 2 x Seven Tools of the Bandit; 1 x Nobleman of Crossout
Side Out: 1 x Bottomless Trap Hole; 1 x Creature Swap; 1 x Amazoness Fighter
3 in, 3 out. A small change to protect your pressure and remove a set wall. Keep ten Amazoness monsters; Tools protects a key attack without shutting off Archers or Call.

title: Archfiend Pandemonium
description:
Three Archfiend General, three Pandemonium, and Terraforming provide access to the Field Spell that supports your Fiends. Archfiend Heiress and destruction by effects turn trades into new threats.

NeoGoat Pro 0.3.2 beta.60 default deck | October 2026

PLAY GUIDE
Keep Pandemonium active, apply pressure with efficient Fiends, and turn the destruction of your own Archfiends into searches.

Game Plan
- Discard Archfiend General to find Pandemonium when needed; once the Field Spell is established, you can keep other copies of General as attackers.
- Start with Archfiend Soldier or Archfiend Heiress to enable Terrorking Archfiend later. That first monster also keeps you from relying on a single threat.
- Use Pandemonium to find a lower-Level Archfiend after destruction by an effect; manage your Traps and LP to sustain this plan over several turns.

Opening Turns
- General plus Terrorking: search for and activate Pandemonium, establish another Archfiend first, and save Terrorking for a later legal Summon.
- With Heiress and protection, accept a battle trade that lets you search for the right Archfiend; do not spend removal just to preserve a small monster.

Key Plays and Synergies
- Mist Archfiend can be Summoned without Tributing, attack, and destroy itself in the End Phase. With Pandemonium, that destruction lets you search for a lower-Level Archfiend.
- Archfiend's Roar revives a threat for 500 LP and destroys it at the end of the turn; if Pandemonium is still active, that destruction can fuel another search.
- Terrorking negates the effects of monsters it destroys by battle. Use it to attack effect-based engines when it can win the battle.
- Desrook Archfiend in hand can bring back Terrorking when it is destroyed and sent to the GY.

Common Mistakes
- Pandemonium removes the Archfiends' Standby Phase payments; it does not prevent Mist's 1000 damage or the 500 LP cost of Archfiend's Roar.
- Terrorking cannot be Normal or Flip Summoned without another Archfiend on your field; Setting it does not make a later Flip Summon legal without that support.
- Heiress searches when sent by an effect or destroyed by battle, not when discarded as the cost of Tribe-Infecting Virus.
- The monster revived by Archfiend's Roar cannot be Tributed. If Pandemonium disappears, Archfiend General destroys itself; protect the Field Spell before relying on several copies.

SIDE DECK GUIDE
Each plan starts from the original deck list and swaps an equal number of cards in and out. Choose a plan based on what you saw in Game 1; do not combine complete plans. These are practice guidelines with verified card counts and legality, not claims of proven performance in human matches.

Side Card Roles
- 2 x Falling Down: While you control a face-up Archfiend, equip this to the best opposing monster and take control of it for as long as it remains equipped. During each opposing Standby Phase, it deals 800 damage to you. This is damage, not a cost, and Pandemonium does not prevent it.
- 1 x Deck Devastation Virus: General, Terrorking, Mist and Skull can pay its cost. It heavily punishes engines built around recruiters, Flip monsters and low-ATK walls.
- 2 x Gemini Imps: Protects your hand against Thestalos, Spirit Reaper, Don Zaloog, Card Destruction and Morphing Jar, replaces itself with a draw, and is still a DARK Fiend.
- 2 x Kycoo the Ghost Destroyer: Applies pressure with 1800 ATK and, while on the field, prevents the opponent from banishing cards from graveyards for Chaos, Miracle Fusion or Dragon's Mirror. Those two Fusion Spells can still use materials exclusively from the field.
- 2 x Dust Tornado: Chainable removal for Field Spells, Future Fusion and floodgates without shutting off your many traps. It also lets you set another Trap.
- 2 x Pulling the Rug: Negates the Normal Summon-triggered effects of Monarchs, Gadgets and Breaker, and destroys them.
- 2 x Mask of Restrict: Shuts down Tribute Summons of Monarchs and other bosses. The corresponding plan removes Skull Archfiend so it does not become a stranded card in your own hand.
- 2 x Royal Oppression: A transformation against Fusion, Dragon and Zombie decks. The plan removes Roar, Premature, Call and Desrook so your intended Special Summon lines are not left exposed to the opponent using Oppression.

Matchup Side Plans

Monarch / Gadget
Side In: 2 x Gemini Imps; 2 x Mask of Restrict; 2 x Pulling the Rug
Side Out: 1 x Skull Archfiend of Lightning; 2 x Mist Archfiend; 1 x Infernalqueen Archfiend; 1 x Desrook Archfiend; 1 x Vilepawn Archfiend
Mask shuts down the Tribute Summon line, Rug answers the summon-triggered effect, and Gemini Imps prevents Thestalos from turning the exchange into advantage.

HERO Fusion / Red-Eyes / Dragon Future / Zombie
Side In: 2 x Royal Oppression; 2 x Dust Tornado; 2 x Kycoo the Ghost Destroyer
Side Out: 2 x Archfiend's Roar; 1 x Premature Burial; 1 x Call of the Haunted; 1 x Desrook Archfiend; 1 x Vilepawn Archfiend
Remove all four revival cards and Desrook, whose resolution outside the Damage Step could be negated by paying 800 LP. Kycoo blocks materials the opponent wants to banish from their graveyard, while Dust answers Future Fusion, Call of the Mummy and Continuous cards.

Chaos Control / Chaos Warrior
Side In: 2 x Kycoo the Ghost Destroyer; 2 x Dust Tornado
Side Out: 1 x Vilepawn Archfiend; 1 x Infernalqueen Archfiend; 1 x Desrook Archfiend; 1 x Mist Archfiend
Kycoo prevents the opponent from banishing LIGHT and DARK monsters from their graveyard, while Dust removes Call, Premature or backrow without interfering with Pandemonium.

Gravekeeper / Spellcaster / Wall Rock
Side In: 1 x Deck Devastation Virus; 2 x Falling Down
Side Out: 1 x Vilepawn Archfiend; 1 x Infernalqueen Archfiend; 1 x Desrook Archfiend
Virus destroys Spy in the hand or face-down, along with low-ATK engines, but a face-up Spy under Necrovalley has 1700 ATK and survives. After its initial resolution, it checks each draw until the end of the opponent's third turn; it does not continually inspect cards added by searches. Falling Down takes a face-up defender or boss while you keep an Archfiend on the field.

Amazoness / Earth Aggro / Harpie
Side In: 2 x Falling Down; 2 x Dust Tornado
Side Out: 2 x Smashing Ground; 1 x Vilepawn Archfiend; 1 x Infernalqueen Archfiend
Falling Down takes the monster instead of merely destroying it, while Dust removes Village, Hunting Ground and set protection.

title: Armed Dragon
description:
Three Flying Kamakiri #1 and three Masked Dragon provide access to Armed Dragon LV3. Three LV5, two LV7, and one Level Up! let you climb the chain, while Cyberdark Keel uses small Dragons in the GY.

NeoGoat Pro 0.3.2 beta.60 default deck | October 2026

PLAY GUIDE
Recruit LV3, reach LV5 with protection, and choose between evolving through battle or accelerating with Level Up!

Game Plan
- Use the six recruiters to survive and set up LV3, ideally during the opponent's turn so it can evolve in your next Standby Phase.
- Save monsters with enough ATK for the effects of LV5 and LV7; do not automatically discard the only evolution piece in your hand.
- Keep Cyberdark Keel's battle plan available while preparing Future Fusion and Dragon's Mirror as finishers.

Opening Turns
- Set Masked Dragon or Flying Kamakiri #1 with protection. If it falls in battle, choose LV3 when it can survive until your Standby Phase.
- With LV5 and Level Up!, first establish a legal LV5 and clear dangerous backrow before turning it into LV7.

Key Plays and Synergies
- LV3 sends itself to the GY in your Standby Phase to summon LV5 from your hand or Deck. An LV5 that destroyed a monster by battle can summon LV7 during the End Phase.
- Level Up! sends a face-up LV monster to the GY and summons the listed monster, ignoring its Summoning conditions; LV5 into LV7 is the highest-impact conversion.
- When Normal Summoned, Cyberdark Keel equips a Level 3 or lower Dragon from the GY, such as LV3, Masked Dragon, or Twin-Headed Behemoth.
- Future Fusion reveals Five-Headed Dragon and sends five Dragons during your first subsequent Standby Phase; Dragon's Mirror can then use those materials.

Common Mistakes
- This list has only one Level Up!, not two. Preserve the natural evolution route and do not build every hand around drawing that copy.
- Future Fusion does not load the GY on activation: it must survive until your first Standby Phase, and the Fusion arrives in the second.
- Cyberdark Keel is a Machine: it is not Dragon material for Five-Headed Dragon and does not enable Stamping Destruction.
- LV7 cannot simply be Summoned with two Tributes or Premature Burial. Sending Sinister Serpent for a LV effect only destroys monsters within its low ATK threshold.

SIDE DECK GUIDE
Each plan starts from the original deck list and swaps an equal number of cards in and out. Choose a plan based on what you saw in Game 1; do not combine complete plans. These are practice guidelines with verified card counts and legality, not claims of proven performance in human matches.

Side Card Roles
- 2 x Soul Release: Removes fuel for opposing Chaos, Gozuki and Dragon's Mirror without using your Normal Summon or shutting down your own graveyard for Keel and Future.
- 2 x Royal Command: Against Spy, Guard, Dekoichi, Crystal Seer and other FLIP monsters. This Main Deck has no FLIP monsters of its own, so it provides persistent negation while Armed develops instead of adding another generic Crossout.
- 2 x Stamping Destruction: Brings the total to three with the Main Deck copy. Remove Necrovalley, Oppression, Drain or traps before leveling up. It requires your own Dragon; Keel is a Machine and is not enough by itself.
- 1 x Giant Trunade: Creates an attack or level-up window against several Continuous cards. It gains tempo rather than destroying cards, and also returns your own Future Fusion and Equip cards.
- 2 x Pulling the Rug: Trades one card for a Monarch or Gadget's Normal Summon-triggered effect without requiring a discard. It does not cover Special Summon-triggered effects or Chaos.
- 2 x Des Wombat: Against burn and Solar Flare, a 1600 ATK threat that prevents effect damage, not battle damage or LP costs.
- 2 x Divine Wrath: Negates Chaos's banishing effect or Fusion Monster effects that My Body cannot cover. Sinister or Dragons you want in the graveyard can pay the discard, but this negation is never free.
- 2 x My Body as a Shield: Preserves an evolved Armed Dragon against mass or single-target destruction. This Quick-Play Spell does not negate your traps, but it does not protect against banishing, returning to the hand or summon negation.

Matchup Side Plans

Chaos Control / Chaos Warrior with an active graveyard
Side In: 2 x Soul Release; 2 x Divine Wrath
Side Out: 1 x Future Fusion; 1 x Level Up!; 1 x Stamping Destruction; 1 x Brain Control
Keep one Future Fusion, all three Flying Kamakiri #1 and every LV monster; remove this list's only Level Up! Soul Release is preventive, while Divine Wrath answers Chaos's effect, not its summon.

Gravekeeper / control with many FLIP monsters
Side In: 2 x Royal Command; 2 x Stamping Destruction; 1 x Giant Trunade
Side Out: 1 x Dragon's Mirror; 1 x Premature Burial; 1 x Call of the Haunted; 1 x Future Fusion; 1 x Brain Control
Royal Command does not affect any of your own Main Deck monsters. Prioritize removing Necrovalley. Stamping Destruction requires a face-up Dragon; Cyberdark Keel alone is not enough.

Monarch / Gadgets
Side In: 2 x Pulling the Rug; 2 x My Body as a Shield
Side Out: 1 x Future Fusion; 1 x Level Up!; 1 x Stamping Destruction; 1 x Dragon's Mirror
Use Rug against Normal Summon-triggered effects. My Body only answers effects that destroy monsters, so it does not cover Thestalos or Mobius. Keep the recruiter core and all three LV5.

Traps and mass destruction
Side In: 2 x Stamping Destruction; 1 x Giant Trunade; 2 x My Body as a Shield
Side Out: 2 x Bottomless Trap Hole; 1 x Future Fusion; 1 x Level Up!; 1 x Brain Control
Remove the less useful summon responses and part of the delayed engine. Keep Mirror Force, Torrential Tribute, Ring of Destruction and Call of the Haunted; the cards brought in protect your development without negating those traps.

Burn / Pyro focused on Solar Flare
Side In: 2 x Des Wombat; 2 x Stamping Destruction; 1 x Giant Trunade
Side Out: 2 x Bottomless Trap Hole; 1 x Mirror Force; 1 x Ring of Destruction; 1 x Brain Control
Wombat does not make costs free. Against battle-focused Pyro, keep Mirror Force and remove a Future Fusion instead. The written plan assumes effect damage or a lock is the main threat.

title: Chaos Control
description:
Two Chaos Sorcerer finish games for a core of six LIGHT monsters, useful DARK monsters, and defensive cards. Spy, Dekoichi, and Tsukuyomi sustain trades while both Attributes build up in the GY.

NeoGoat Pro 0.3.2 beta.60 default deck | October 2026

PLAY GUIDE
Trade patiently, reuse Flip Effects, and preserve LIGHT/DARK material so Chaos Sorcerer arrives with a specific job.

Game Plan
- Build the GY through useful battles and effects; do not needlessly sacrifice your six LIGHT monsters just to summon Chaos a turn earlier.
- Protect Spy or Dekoichi when they can provide another card or a second monster, and use Tsukuyomi to reuse an effect when the field allows it.
- Summon Chaos Sorcerer to remove a face-up threat or finish through attacks; count the fuel needed for the second copy.

Opening Turns
- With Thunder Dragon, discard one copy to search for the other if it is still in the Deck. With only two copies, this is not a two-card search.
- A Set Spy or Dekoichi plus protection lets you open without revealing Chaos. Against a known threat, ROTA can find D.D. Warrior Lady or Exiled Force.

Key Plays and Synergies
- Book of Moon followed by Nobleman of Crossout removes a monster that was initially face-up, provided both effects can resolve.
- Tsukuyomi can Set Spy or Dekoichi again for reuse on a later turn; it also turns an opposing boss into a target you can attack through its DEF.
- Raigeki Break and Tribe-Infecting Virus turn a spare discard into interaction. Night Assailant can recover another Flip monster already in the GY.
- Kycoo the Ghost Destroyer stops the opponent from banishing cards from the GYs while it is face-up, and can remove materials when it deals damage.

Common Mistakes
- Chaos Sorcerer cannot attack in the turn it activates its banishing effect; do not count those 2300 when calculating lethal damage.
- Night Assailant cannot recover itself. Sinister Serpent has a later banishing effect and does not guarantee endless discards.
- Card Destruction can fix the opponent's hand and load their GY; use it for a concrete benefit, not just because it is available.
- Nobleman on an opposing Spy can also banish your own copies of Spy from the Deck; assess the trade before resolving it.

SIDE DECK GUIDE
Each plan starts from the original deck list and swaps an equal number of cards in and out. Choose a plan based on what you saw in Game 1; do not combine complete plans. These are practice guidelines with verified card counts and legality, not claims of proven performance in human matches.

Side Card Roles
- 2 x Kycoo the Ghost Destroyer: Brings the total to three with the Main Deck copy: DARK pressure and a block on opposing graveyard banishing against Chaos, Gozuki and graveyard-based Fusions, without stopping your own Chaos. Miracle Fusion and Dragon's Mirror can still use only materials on the field. The two additional copies replace slow DARK monsters, not LIGHTs.
- 2 x Soul Release: Proactively removes up to five cards before Sorcerer, Book of Life or Miracle Fusion can use them. Two copies help you draw it in time. It is not quick interaction: target the opposing graveyard rather than removing your own materials.
- 2 x Cipher Soldier: A battle answer to Blade Knight, Don and Amazoness without spending the Chaos engine. Two copies improve the chance of drawing it naturally; it is neither LIGHT nor searchable with ROTA.
- 2 x Dust Tornado: A reactive answer to Decree, Necrovalley and Continuous Traps that keeps your nine traps active. Two copies reinforce Heavy and MST without requiring another Normal Summon.
- 2 x Pulling the Rug: Negates the Normal Summon-triggered effects of Gadgets and Monarchs, and destroys them. Two copies check their early advantage; it does not cover Special Summons or graveyard effects.
- 2 x Des Wombat: Two monsters against effect damage let you attack while clearing the lock; they do not prevent battle damage. Remove redundant battle defense, not LIGHT monsters.
- 1 x Mirage Dragon: An additional LIGHT that blocks opposing trap activations during the Battle Phase, such as Mirror Force and Sakuretsu, without negating your own traps. One copy avoids crowding your Normal Summons. It does not negate active traps or protect its own summon.
- 1 x Divine Wrath: Answers monster effects that later removal cannot solve, including graveyard effects. Only one copy, since the deck already has Tribe and two Raigeki Break. Prefer discarding Serpent or a redundant Thunder; discard Night Assailant only if another FLIP monster can be recovered from the graveyard.
- 1 x Nobleman of Crossout: A second copy overall for set defenders and FLIP engines. One is enough alongside the two existing Book of Moon. Avoid using it automatically in a Spy mirror, since it can also banish your own Spies from the Deck.

Matchup Side Plans

Chaos / Zombie / graveyard decks
Side In: 2 x Kycoo the Ghost Destroyer; 2 x Soul Release; 1 x Divine Wrath
Side Out: 1 x Card Destruction; 1 x Don Zaloog; 2 x Gravekeeper's Spy; 1 x Nobleman of Crossout
5 in, 5 out. Keep all six LIGHT monsters and both Sorcerers; Kycoo replaces slow DARKs. Soul Release is preventive, while Wrath supplies the interruption. Do not also remove Thunder Dragons or add Banisher.

Battle-focused Warrior / Amazoness
Side In: 2 x Cipher Soldier; 1 x Divine Wrath
Side Out: 1 x Kycoo the Ghost Destroyer; 1 x Card Destruction; 1 x Spirit Reaper
3 in, 3 out. Cipher wins battles; Wrath answers monster effects, not Village's Spell effect. Do not give the opponent graveyard or hand resources with Card Destruction. Keep all six LIGHT monsters, your removal and both Spies.

Gadget Monarch
Side In: 2 x Pulling the Rug; 1 x Divine Wrath
Side Out: 1 x Nobleman of Crossout; 1 x Dekoichi the Battlechanted Locomotive; 1 x Card Destruction

title: Chaos Warrior
description:
Three Blade Knight, two Reflect Bounder, one D.D. Warrior Lady, and Ninja Grandmaster Sasuke supply the seven LIGHT monsters in this aggressive core. Warriors and removal clear the way for two Chaos Sorcerer without relying on a slow draw engine.

NeoGoat Pro 0.3.2 beta.60 default deck | October 2026

PLAY GUIDE
Win the early battles, force answers, and turn used LIGHT/DARK monsters into a second wave of Chaos.

Game Plan
- Present one protected attacker and keep the next in hand; Shrink and Book of Moon help win a battle without overextending.
- Use Reinforcement of the Army to find the tool for the opposing field: Exiled Force, Mystic Swordsman LV2, or a useful LIGHT monster.
- Use the two Chaos Sorcerer after your Warriors have drawn out removal and supplied both Attributes, without spending all the materials at once.

Opening Turns
- Blade Knight plus protection applies pressure from the first turn. Do not empty your hand just to meet its conditions.
- Against Set monsters, hold Mystic Swordsman LV2 or Nobleman of Crossout; against a face-up Defense Position monster, Ninja Grandmaster Sasuke offers another route.

Key Plays and Synergies
- Shrink lets Don Zaloog win a battle and deal damage to activate its hand effect; it can also preserve your LIGHT monsters for another battle.
- Book of Moon turns a monster face-down for Mystic Swordsman LV2 or Nobleman, each with its own activation timing.
- Zombyra the Dark attacks over many early monsters; Book of Moon can reset its ATK losses when Setting it again is useful.
- Chaos Sorcerer removes a face-up threat that battle cannot answer, while another Warrior remains available to attack.

Common Mistakes
- Zombyra cannot attack directly and loses 200 ATK after destroying a monster by battle; calculate later battles using its current ATK.
- Blade Knight only gains ATK with one card or fewer in hand, and only negates Flip Effects when its condition of controlling no other monsters is met.
- The Main Deck's only Flip monster is one Night Assailant; discarding it does not produce a recovery on its own.
- Do not cut the LIGHT package when siding without checking your access to Chaos. Sorcerer loses its attack for the turn if it uses its banishing effect.

SIDE DECK GUIDE
Each plan starts from the original deck list and swaps an equal number of cards in and out. Choose a plan based on what you saw in Game 1; do not combine complete plans. These are practice guidelines with verified card counts and legality, not claims of proven performance in human matches.

Side Card Roles
- 2 x Kycoo the Ghost Destroyer: Brings the total to three to win the graveyard race while preserving DARK count. It applies 1800 ATK pressure without stopping your own Sorcerer; two copies replace less useful threats in this matchup. It only prevents the opponent from banishing from graveyards, so Miracle Fusion and Dragon's Mirror can still use materials exclusively on the field.
- 2 x Soul Release: Removes Chaos materials and revival targets before they are used. Two copies reinforce the Kycoo plan without subjecting your own graveyard to continuous banishing.
- 2 x Dust Tornado: Removes locks, Decree and Field Spells without shutting down Bottomless, Sakuretsu, Mirror Force or Call. Quick responses are preferred over another Tribute monster competing for the Normal Summon.
- 2 x Seven Tools of the Bandit: Protects a key summon or attack from Counter Traps and battle traps, and can also negate Decree's activation. Two copies support your pressure without disabling your eight traps. Each use costs 1000 LP.
- 2 x Cipher Soldier: Provides favorable battle exchanges against Warriors and Amazoness, even under pressure. It is not a Warrior, so ROTA cannot search it; it does not replace the Blade and Sasuke core.
- 2 x Pulling the Rug: Stops Gadget and Monarch effects. Two copies rather than three leave room for graveyard and trap answers. Do not bring it in by default against Fusions or recruiters.
- 2 x Des Wombat: Two chances to establish protection from effect damage and attack. Its Type and Attribute do not fuel Chaos, so replace battle Spells and Traps rather than LIGHT monsters.
- 1 x Chaos Trap Hole: An additional answer to Chaos Sorcerer's inherent Special Summon and the Normal or Flip Summon of LIGHT and DARK monsters. One copy because it costs 2000 LP. It cannot be relied on to negate Ritual or Fusion Summons performed within a Chain.

Warrior / Amazoness with battle traps
Side In: 2 x Cipher Soldier; 2 x Seven Tools of the Bandit
Side Out: 1 x Mystic Swordsman LV2; 2 x Nobleman of Crossout; 1 x Night Assailant
4 in, 4 out. Keep every Blade Knight, both Sorcerers, all seven LIGHTs and seven DARKs. Cipher stabilizes battles, while Tools protects your advance. Do not spend Tools and 1000 LP on an irrelevant exchange.

Gadget Monarch
Side In: 2 x Pulling the Rug
Side Out: 2 x Nobleman of Crossout
2 in, 2 out. A minimal change that preserves Warrior pressure and monster removal. Rug stops the opponent from gaining advantage from their Normal Summon.

Burn / stall
Side In: 2 x Des Wombat; 2 x Dust Tornado; 2 x Seven Tools of the Bandit
Side Out: 2 x Bottomless Trap Hole; 1 x Brain Control; 2 x Smashing Ground; 1 x Exiled Force
6 in, 6 out. Replace monster removal with LP protection and ways to clear backrow. All seven LIGHTs stay intact. Reserve Tools for a trap that will meaningfully change the turn.

Trap-heavy control / VanDalgyon
Side In: 2 x Dust Tornado; 2 x Seven Tools of the Bandit
Side Out: 2 x Nobleman of Crossout; 1 x Mystic Swordsman LV2; 1 x Night Assailant
4 in, 4 out. Dust forces a response before you attack; Tools protects the crucial action without invalidating your own traps. Do not negate an irrelevant Counter Trap merely to continue a chain of exchanges.

title: Dragon Future

description:
An entirely Dragon monster lineup supports three Totem Dragon, two Future Fusion, and two Dragon's Mirror. The list can win through ordinary pressure, evolve Horus, or finish with Five-Headed Dragon.

NeoGoat Pro 0.3.2 beta.60 default deck | October 2026

PLAY GUIDE
Develop small Dragons, prepare a useful GY, and choose the boss that answers the field.

Game Plan
- Start with Masked Dragon, Luster Dragon, or Mirage Dragon; force the opponent to spend answers while Future Fusion prepares the next wave.
- Keep Totem Dragon in the GY and your field empty when you want to revive it in your Standby Phase; it can count as two Tributes for a Dragon.
- Choose Horus to control Spells or Five-Headed Dragon for ATK pressure. Save Dimension Fusion for enough banished monsters to justify 2000 LP.

Opening Turns
- With Future Fusion and protection, activate the Continuous Spell early and protect the waiting turn; check that five Dragons remain in the Deck for its first Standby Phase.
- Foolish Burial can send Totem Dragon if you plan to revive it in a later Standby Phase with an empty field, or a Dragon you need to recover with another card.

Key Plays and Synergies
- Future Fusion loads five Dragons by revealing Five-Headed Dragon during your first subsequent Standby Phase. Dragon's Mirror turns field or GY materials into another Fusion.
- Totem Dragon can count as two Tributes for Tyrant Dragon; a Totem revived by its own effect is banished when it leaves the field.
- Horus the Black Flame Dragon LV6 can summon LV8 in the End Phase after destroying a monster by battle; LV8 lets you respond to Spell activations.
- Mirage Dragon prevents the opponent from activating Traps during the Battle Phase; use it to support the decisive attack.

Common Mistakes
- Future Fusion does not send materials on activation, and its Fusion is destroyed if the Continuous Spell leaves the field. Your own Heavy Storm can break that link.
- Totem requires an empty field and no non-Dragon monsters in your GY; check that condition after bringing in monsters from the Side Deck.
- Horus LV6 is unaffected by Spells, including your own Book of Moon and other Spells. LV8 requires its Summoning route and cannot be brought back with ordinary revival.
- Dimension Fusion also returns the opponent's banished monsters. Mirage Dragon does not remove already-active Continuous Traps or protect you outside battle.

SIDE DECK GUIDE
Each plan starts from the original deck list and swaps an equal number of cards in and out. Choose a plan based on what you saw in Game 1; do not combine complete plans. These are practice guidelines with verified card counts and legality, not claims of proven performance in human matches.

Side Card Roles
- 2 x Soul Release: A graveyard answer that avoids adding non-Dragons that would block Totem. Do not use it before Dimension Fusion if that would let the opponent recover strong banished monsters.
- 2 x Nobleman of Crossout: Removes Spy, Guard and FLIP monsters without waiting for your Dragons to win a battle. There are no same-name FLIP monsters of your own to lose.
- 2 x Stamping Destruction: Up to three copies with the Main Deck card to handle Continuous cards and backrow. Every Main Deck monster is a Dragon.

- 2 x Pulling the Rug: Prevents Monarchs and Gadgets from gaining advantage through their Normal Summon-triggered effects while you prepare your own Tribute Summons.
- 2 x Royal Decree: Only for the anti-trap transformation that removes ALL SIX original traps. Do not add it alongside Call, Bottomless, Compulsory or Rug.
- 1 x Mirage Dragon: A third Normal Summonable Dragon with 1600 ATK that blocks opposing trap activations during battle. It does not replace Decree against traps outside the Battle Phase or against Continuous Traps that are already active.
- 2 x Compulsory Evacuation Device: Reactive return-to-hand removal against Chaos, Ritual and Fusion monsters without battling or destroying them. It offsets the slowness of your Tribute monsters and stays out of the Decree plan.
- 1 x My Body as a Shield: Protects the investment in a Tribute or Fusion monster against destruction. A single supporting copy avoids doubling up on LP costs.

Trap-heavy decks / trap burn: full transformation
Side In: 2 x Royal Decree; 2 x Stamping Destruction; 1 x Giant Trunade; 1 x Mirage Dragon
Side Out: 2 x Bottomless Trap Hole; 1 x Mirror Force; 1 x Torrential Tribute; 1 x Ring of Destruction; 1 x Call of the Haunted
Exactly two traps remain: both Decrees. No card brought in adds a non-Dragon monster. Do not also bring in Rug or Compulsory from other plans. Mirage covers the Battle Phase even without drawing Decree, but it does not stop burn during the Main Phase.

Chaos / Zombie / graveyard decks
Side In: 2 x Soul Release; 2 x Compulsory Evacuation Device
Side Out: 1 x Dimension Fusion; 1 x Future Fusion; 1 x Stamping Destruction; 1 x Tyrant Dragon
Remove Dimension Fusion so it does not return the opponent's monsters banished by Soul Release. Keep Totem and the remaining Tribute monsters. Compulsory does not belong alongside Decree.

Monarch / Gadgets
Side In: 2 x Pulling the Rug; 1 x My Body as a Shield
Side Out: 1 x Dimension Fusion; 1 x Dragon's Mirror; 1 x Future Fusion
Keep one Dragon's Mirror and one Future Fusion. Rug negates Normal Summon-triggered effects; My Body protects against destruction, not discarding, banishing or returning cards to the hand.

FLIP monsters without Necrovalley
Side In: 2 x Nobleman of Crossout
Side Out: 2 x Bottomless Trap Hole
A small change that answers set monsters instead of waiting for a face-up summon with enough ATK.

Gravekeeper with Necrovalley and Oppression
Side In: 2 x Stamping Destruction; 1 x Giant Trunade; 2 x Nobleman of Crossout
Side Out: 1 x Dimension Fusion; 1 x Dragon's Mirror; 1 x Future Fusion; 1 x Call of the Haunted; 1 x Premature Burial
Reduce the cards that depend on the graveyard. The remaining Totems need Necrovalley removed before reviving themselves. Once on the field, they can still count as two Tributes while the opponent keeps Necrovalley, subject to their effect's requirements.

- Use Rat and Momonga to maintain field presence; Momonga's LP gain helps fund Injection Fairy Lily and Green Baboon.
- Apply pressure with a large attacker and protection. Rush Recklessly or Book of Moon can win a trade without spending another monster.
- Banish expendable EARTH monsters for Gigantes or The Rock Spirit, creating a second threat after the opponent has used their main answer.

Opening Turns
- A Set Rat lets you choose between more field presence, Injection Fairy Lily, or Exiled Force once you know the battle situation.
- With Gorilla and protection, attack carefully; with Momonga and Creature Swap, prepare the exchange when the opponent can only give you a valuable monster.

Key Plays and Synergies
- Creature Swap gives away Giant Rat or Nimble Momonga and lets you attack it with the monster you receive, using its effect when it reaches your GY.
- Enraged Battle Ox grants piercing to your Beast, Beast-Warrior, and Winged Beast monsters; combine it with Gorilla to punish defenders.
- Injection Fairy Lily can pay 2000 LP during damage calculation to overcome a boss; also account for Premature Burial's payment and Ring of Destruction's damage.
- If a face-up Beast is destroyed by an effect and sent to the GY outside the Damage Step, Green Baboon can arrive from your hand or GY for 1000 LP.

Common Mistakes
- Green Baboon cannot be Summoned following battle destruction within the Damage Step. Do not base its arrival on deliberately losing Rat or Momonga there.
- Gorilla must attack if able and destroys itself in face-up Defense Position; Book of Moon only leaves it face-down temporarily.
- Goblin Attack Force changes to Defense Position after attacking and is restricted from changing position; consider the next turn before leaving it exposed.
- Gigantes destroyed by battle also wipes out your Spells and Traps. The Rock Spirit only gains its 300 ATK during the opponent's Battle Phase.

SIDE DECK GUIDE

- 2 x Des Wombat: Two copies against burn while preserving Momonga. Its 1600 ATK prevents Rat from summoning it. Keeps the attack plan and protects LP, but does not prevent battle damage.
- 2 x Pulling the Rug: Negates the advantage generated by Gadget and Monarch Normal Summon effects, which cannot be solved simply by increasing ATK. Two copies for this specific matchup.
- 1 x Enemy Controller: One extra flexible interaction card to change an attacker's position or take a boss and finish the game. It can use a spare recruiter as a Tribute, but Tributing that monster does NOT trigger its battle effect.

- 1 x Nightmare Penguin: Mother Grizzly can summon it because it has 900 ATK. While face-up, it raises Hydrogeddon from 1600 to 1800 ATK. Being summoned by Grizzly does not trigger its flip effect; it must be set and then flipped face-up to return an opposing card.

Side Out: 1 x Shrink; 1 x Enemy Controller; 1 x Smashing Ground
Three dedicated Spell and Trap answers replace less reliable battle interaction. Mobius still counts as WATER once it reaches the graveyard.

Wombat stops the effect-damage clock, while Dust removes Molten Destruction or Continuous cards before they build advantage.

Chaos Warrior / Earth Aggro / battle control without graveyard hate

title: Gravekeeper
description:
Three Necrovalley, three Commandant, and Terraforming provide access to the Field Spell. Spy, Guard, and Assailant maintain the field while GY restrictions limit Chaos and revival routes.

NeoGoat Pro 0.3.2 beta.60 default deck | October 2026

PLAY GUIDE
Establish Necrovalley, build field presence with Spy, and turn your stat advantage into safe attacks.

Game Plan
- Search for Necrovalley when missing, and keep another way to find it after removal; do not spend every Commandant if you need attackers.
- Protect Spy to summon the right Gravekeeper: another body, Guard for a future turn, or an attacker that benefits from the Field Spell.
- Save Dust Tornado and Solemn Judgment for cards that dismantle Necrovalley or change the damage race, rather than answering every minor play.

Opening Turns
- A Set Spy with Necrovalley and protection creates a 2500 DEF defender and threatens a second monster if flipped.
- Commandant can search for Necrovalley or attack with 2100 ATK under it; decide based on whether the Field Spell is already available.

Key Plays and Synergies
- Assailant changes a face-up opposing monster's battle position when declaring an attack with Necrovalley active; Spear Soldier adds piercing damage against defenders.
- Tsukuyomi Sets Spy or Guard again so you can reuse its effect when it can be flipped once more.
- Rite of Spirit revives a Gravekeeper despite Necrovalley. A Tribute Summoned Chief can bring back another and makes your GY unaffected by the Field Spell.
- Assailant, Spear Soldier, Ambusher, or Chief under Necrovalley can pay for Deck Devastation Virus; confirm the chosen monster is still DARK and has at least 2000 ATK.

Common Mistakes
- Commandant is EARTH: even at 2100 ATK, it cannot pay for Deck Devastation Virus. Use a valid DARK monster such as Chief with Necrovalley.
- Spy searches for monsters with 1500 ATK or less in the Deck; Necrovalley does not increase their ATK there, and Commandant's 1600 ATK makes it ineligible.
- Heavy Storm destroys your own Necrovalley. Plan whether the clear lets you finish the game or whether you need a replacement copy first.
- Nobleman of Crossout on an opposing Spy or Guard can banish your copies from the Deck; Rite cannot help a monster that is already banished.

SIDE DECK GUIDE
Each plan starts from the original deck list and swaps an equal number of cards in and out. Choose a plan based on what you saw in Game 1; do not combine complete plans. These are practice guidelines with verified card counts and legality, not claims of proven performance in human matches.

Side Card Roles
- 2 x Royal Oppression: Two copies for the anti-Special Summon plan; remove Chief and both Rite of Spirit. There is still a conflict with voluntarily Flip Summoning Spy outside the Damage Step. Establish your monsters before activating Oppression.
- 2 x Rivalry of Warlords: The entire Main Deck monster lineup is Spellcaster, so two copies punish mixed Types in Chaos and Warrior without requiring an engine transformation. Do not combine this package with Wombat or Mobius, which would prevent you from deploying Spellcasters.
- 2 x Pulling the Rug: Answers Monarchs and Gadgets before they gain advantage. Two copies are enough alongside the Main Deck Bottomless Traps, leaving room for Field Spell answers.
- 1 x Mobius the Frost Monarch: One Tribute monster that turns a spare Spy into two backrow removals, especially against locks. A single copy avoids clogging the hand. It cannot coexist with Spellcasters under Rivalry, so they belong in separate plans.
- 2 x Des Wombat: Necrovalley alone is not enough against burn. Two copies help establish protection with an attacker. Spy cannot summon them, and they do not belong in the Rivalry plan.
- 1 x Dust Tornado: A third copy overall for Decree and persistent locks. Only one is needed because the Main Deck already has two, Heavy Storm and MST.
- 1 x Nobleman of Crossout: A second copy for Wall Rock and set defenders without overloading on removal. Not an automatic choice in a Spy mirror: it would also banish your own copies from the Deck.
- 1 x Gemini Imps: Hand-based protection against Mazera or Thestalos discarding. It replaces itself if it negates and destroys. One copy supports the Rug plan; do not summon it as a Fiend while using Rivalry.
- 2 x Spell Shattering Arrow: A quick answer to opposing Future Fusion, Field Spells and Continuous Spells that preserves Necrovalley. Two copies let you act before Future resolves. It does not destroy traps or negate Normal Spells.
- 1 x Seven Tools of the Bandit: Focused protection against Decree's activation or a Counter Trap that would stop you from breaking a lock. One copy because of the LP cost and because Dust already covers active traps.

Matchup Side Plans

Fusion / Special Summons and Future Fusion
Side In: 2 x Royal Oppression; 2 x Spell Shattering Arrow
Side Out: 2 x Rite of Spirit; 1 x Gravekeeper's Chief; 1 x Deck Devastation Virus
4 in, 4 out. Establish your board before applying the lock; Oppression affects both players. Do not voluntarily Flip Summon Spy expecting the opponent to allow its effect. Battle-triggered recruitment during the Damage Step normally does not offer an Oppression window. Arrow removes Future before it resolves.

Chaos / mixed-Type decks
Side In: 2 x Rivalry of Warlords
Side Out: 1 x Rite of Spirit; 1 x Gravekeeper's Chief
2 in, 2 out. Keep every Spellcaster and one Rite of Spirit. Remove Chief so your own graveyard stays sealed. Maintain Necrovalley and do not also bring in Mobius or Wombat. Rivalry does not stop an opposing board whose monsters all share a Type.

Gadget Monarch / Mazera discard
Side In: 2 x Pulling the Rug; 1 x Gemini Imps
Side Out: 1 x Gravekeeper's Chief; 1 x Gravekeeper's Guard; 1 x Nobleman of Crossout
3 in, 3 out. Rug answers Gadget and Monarch, while Gemini covers Thestalos and Mazera from the hand. Rug does NOT negate Mazera's Special Summon. Necrovalley does not stop you from sending Gemini from the hand as a cost. Keep Deck Devastation Virus because it is highly valuable against Gadgets.

Burn / trap locks
Side In: 2 x Des Wombat; 1 x Dust Tornado; 1 x Mobius the Frost Monarch; 1 x Seven Tools of the Bandit
Side Out: 3 x Bottomless Trap Hole; 1 x Brain Control; 1 x Deck Devastation Virus
5 in, 5 out. No Rivalry or Oppression in this plan. Spy provides a Tribute for Mobius, Wombat protects LP, and three Dust Tornado in total handle the lock without negating your own traps.

Wall Rock / defenders and Continuous Spells
Side In: 1 x Nobleman of Crossout; 2 x Spell Shattering Arrow; 1 x Mobius the Frost Monarch; 1 x Seven Tools of the Bandit
Side Out: 3 x Bottomless Trap Hole; 1 x Brain Control; 1 x Gravekeeper's Chief
5 in, 5 out. Crossout removes set defenders, Arrow handles Weapon Change or Canyon, and Mobius clears backrow. Keep Deck Devastation Virus, which is very useful against low-ATK walls, along with Spy, Ambusher and both Rite of Spirit. Leave out Rivalry so the Tribute Summon remains legal. Do not blindly use the same plan against other Spy decks.

title: Harpie Lady
description:
Three Harpie Lady 1, three Harpie Queen, and two Harpie Oracle support Hunting Ground and Hysteric Party. Elegant Egotist extends your plays, and Swallow's Nest turns a Level 4 Winged Beast into the right piece.

NeoGoat Pro 0.3.2 beta.60 default deck | October 2026

PLAY GUIDE
Use Hunting Ground to gain value from each Summon and save Hysteric Party as a second wave.

Game Plan
- Search for Harpies' Hunting Ground with Queen when there is backrow to destroy; keep Queen as an attacker when the Field Spell would not have a useful target.
- Develop your Harpies without spending the whole hand. Lady 1 boosts WIND monsters and helps smaller bodies compete in battle.
- Prepare Hysteric Party with several Harpies in the GY and a card to discard so you can restore pressure after a board clear.

Opening Turns
- Queen can search for Hunting Ground; with another Harpie ready to summon, activate the Field Spell first if there is a worthwhile target.
- Flying Kamakiri #1 can summon Harpie Lady 1 or Oracle after falling in battle, preserving your Normal Summon for the next turn.

Key Plays and Synergies
- Queen or Oracle on the field is named Harpie Lady and enables Elegant Egotist; Egotist summons Lady 1 or Sisters from your hand or Deck.
- Sisters lets you summon Oracle from your hand. In the End Phase, Oracle can recover Elegant Egotist or Hunting Ground because they mention Harpie Lady Sisters.
- Swallow's Nest Tributes a face-up Winged Beast and summons another of the same Level; replacing a Level 4 Harpie with Queen or Oracle can trigger the Field Spell again.
- Icarus Attack turns a Winged Beast into the destruction of two cards. Hysteric Party also revives Queen and Oracle, whose names are Harpie Lady in the GY.

Common Mistakes
- Hunting Ground is mandatory: if no opposing backrow remains, you may have to destroy your own card, including the Field Spell itself.
- Queen is not named Harpie Lady in the Deck, so Elegant Egotist cannot summon it from there. Swallow's Nest can access it through Type and Level.
- Summoning several Harpies simultaneously with Party does not trigger Hunting Ground separately for each monster.
- Lady 1 boosts every WIND monster, including the opponent's. Icarus requires two targets, and Sisters must first be properly Summoned with Elegant Egotist.

SIDE DECK GUIDE
Each plan starts from the original deck list and swaps an equal number of cards in and out. Choose a plan based on what you saw in Game 1; do not combine complete plans. These are practice guidelines with verified card counts and legality, not claims of proven performance in human matches.

Side Card Roles
- 2 x Kycoo the Ghost Destroyer: An 1800 ATK threat that prevents the opponent from banishing from the GYs for Chaos/Gozuki/Miracle; Miracle Fusion and Dragon's Mirror can still use only field materials. Two copies provide access without a searcher. It is neither WIND nor Winged Beast, so it replaces support cards, not the Harpies.
- 2 x Des Wombat: Two copies against effect damage let you keep attacking while HHG clears the way. Kamakiri cannot search it, and it does not protect against battle damage.
- 2 x Dust Tornado: Answers Oppression/Decree or Field Spells before Hunting Ground is established. Two copies keep you from relying entirely on summoning a Harpie to remove the Trap that prevents that summon.
- 2 x Anti-Spell Fragrance: A tempo plan against Spell engines: the opponent's Set Spells become Hunting Ground targets. Two copies help find it early. It also delays your own Egotist, Nest and Book, so establish your plays first.
- 2 x Pulling the Rug: Stops Gadget/Monarch effects from overwhelming the Harpies. It does not negate Fusions or recruiters; two copies fill that specific role.
- 1 x Enemy Controller: Changes battle position against combat threats, or takes control of a monster to finish with a wide board. One copy because it overlaps with the two Books; the Tribute is a cost and does not generate value through Hunting Ground.
- 1 x Spell Shattering Arrow: An additional immediate answer to Future Fusion/Field Spells without returning or destroying your own HHG. One copy because HHG/Queen/Heavy/MST already provide removal; it does not answer Traps.
- 2 x Seven Tools of the Bandit: Protects your opening development or a decisive attack from Traps without shutting off Party/Icarus/Call. Two copies for backrow matchups; pay 1000 only when it preserves a meaningful play.
- 1 x Lightning Vortex: The only additional board wipe for a wide face-up board. It can discard a Harpie for Party to revive later, but that remains a real cost, and it does not destroy Set monsters.

Matchup Side Plans

Chaos / GY-based Zombie
Side In: 2 x Kycoo the Ghost Destroyer
Side Out: 1 x Hunter Owl; 1 x Garuda the Wind Spirit
2 in, 2 out. Keeps all Harpies, Kamakiri, Egotist, Nest and Party. Nine Winged Beasts remain, including eight Level 4 monsters for Nest; Kycoo is not a valid Tribute or search target for those effects.

Gadget Monarch
Side In: 2 x Pulling the Rug
Side Out: 1 x Nobleman of Crossout; 1 x Hunter Owl
2 in, 2 out. Keeps Sisters/Oracle/Egotist intact: Rug checks the advantage from opposing Normal Summons while your own engine develops.

Spell-heavy Fusion / Ritual
Side In: 2 x Anti-Spell Fragrance; 1 x Spell Shattering Arrow
Side Out: 1 x Nobleman of Crossout; 1 x Smashing Ground; 1 x Hunter Owl
3 in, 3 out. Activate HHG and prepare your first wave and Set Spells before Fragrance. All your own Spells are subject to the delay, including Nest. HHG may be forced to destroy one of your own Spells/Traps if no other target is available: do not pile up Field Spells blindly.

Burn / stall
Side In: 2 x Des Wombat; 2 x Dust Tornado; 1 x Spell Shattering Arrow; 2 x Seven Tools of the Bandit
Side Out: 2 x Bottomless Trap Hole; 2 x Smashing Ground; 1 x Mirror Force; 1 x Ring of Destruction; 1 x Nobleman of Crossout
7 in, 7 out. Keeps the full Harpie engine and Icarus/Party instead of negating your own Traps. Wombat prevents burn damage, while Arrow/Dust/HHG break the lock; removing Ring avoids dangerous self-damage.

Earth / Amazoness with an established board and battle Traps
Side In: 1 x Lightning Vortex; 1 x Enemy Controller; 2 x Seven Tools of the Bandit
Side Out: 1 x Hunter Owl; 1 x Harpies' Hunting Ground; 1 x Call of the Haunted; 1 x Hysteric Party
4 in, 4 out. Keeps both Egotists, both Nests, Sisters, both Oracles and one Party; trades slow revival for immediate interaction. Vortex only hits face-up monsters; Controller can open an attack without Tributing, or take control to finish. Do not treat Tools as an automatic tax on every attack.

title: HERO Fusion
description:
Fifteen different Fusions provide answers to a range of fields. Three E - Emergency Call, three King of the Swamp, and Prisma find or prepare materials for Polymerization, Miracle Fusion, and the two Future Fusion.

NeoGoat Pro 0.3.2 beta.60 default deck | October 2026

PLAY GUIDE
Choose the useful Fusion first, gather its exact materials, and save Miracle Fusion as a second wave.

Game Plan
- Use E - Emergency Call and Reinforcement of the Army to complete the play your hand actually supports: Prisma, a missing material, or a HERO that can battle.
- Do not fuse just because you can. Gaia weakens a threat, Plasma Vice removes Attack Position monsters, and Wildedge punishes multiple monsters; choose for the field.
- Build up materials through battles, Prisma, and Polymerization before spending Miracle Fusion, letting you present threats across more than one turn.

Opening Turns
- King of the Swamp can search for Polymerization; first check whether you need to keep it in hand as a substitute for a named material.
- Future Fusion must survive until your first Standby Phase to send materials. Opening with Woodsman and protection can prepare Polymerization for the following turn.

Key Plays and Synergies
- Prisma reveals a Fusion and sends a material whose name is specifically listed on it; Prisma takes that name until the End Phase.
- King of the Swamp substitutes for one specifically named material. For example, alongside Sparkman it can replace Flame Wingman for Shining Flare Wingman.
- Miracle Fusion banishes materials from your field or GY; Gaia uses a HERO and an EARTH monster, while Nova Master uses a HERO and a FIRE monster.
- Necroshade in the GY enables a Normal Summon without Tributes for a high-Level HERO such as Bladedge, once through that effect.

Common Mistakes
- Royal Decree also negates your Mirror Force, Torrential Tribute, and Ring of Destruction; decide when to use those Traps before keeping Decree active.
- Prisma cannot send a generic material just because the requirement says HERO, EARTH, or FIRE; King of the Swamp cannot substitute for generic requirements either.
- Future Fusion is delayed, and Fusions that require a Fusion Summon cannot simply be recovered with Premature Burial.
- Do not use Miracle to spend every material needed for another Fusion. Check for Necrovalley or an opposing Kycoo before planning to banish from the GY.

SIDE DECK GUIDE
Each plan starts from the original deck list and swaps an equal number of cards in and out. Choose a plan based on what you saw in Game 1; do not combine complete plans. These are practice guidelines with verified card counts and legality, not claims of proven performance in human matches.

Side Card Roles
- 2 x Hero Blast: Recovers Sparkman or other Normal HERO monsters for Polymerization and destroys a face-up opposing monster whose ATK is no higher than the recovered monster's. Sparkman sets the ceiling at 1600, so it cannot destroy Chaos or Monarch. Bring it in only when removing both Decrees.
- 1 x Elemental HERO Wildheart: A second Wildheart, searchable with E-Call or ROTA. It applies trap-immune pressure and is an actual material for Wildedge, Wild Wingman, Necroid Shaman and Gaia.
- 2 x De-Fusion: Removes opposing Fusions without destroying them and can protect your own Fusion from a targeted effect. Recovering its materials requires all the materials actually used to be in the graveyard, along with enough space. Miracle usually banishes them, and Metamorphosis does not enable this material recovery.
- 2 x Soul Release: Removes fuel for opposing Chaos, Zombie and Fusion decks while preserving your graveyard for Miracle. As a Spell, it does not conflict with Decree.
- 2 x Nobleman of Crossout: Removes Spy, Guard and FLIP monsters that would otherwise force you to spend Fusions. Be careful against Morphing Jar: your Main Deck also uses it, and your copy will be banished if it is still in the Deck.
- 2 x Spiritualism: An immediate, non-negatable answer to Necrovalley, Oppression, Drain or an attack lock. It opens a Fusion window without waiting for Dust and works under your own Decree. It only returns the card; it does not remove it permanently.
- 2 x Des Wombat: For effect damage and burn. It is not HERO material, so it stays in the Side Deck until needed. Preserve E-Call, the Normal Monsters and the Fusion routes.
- 2 x Pulling the Rug: Monarchs and Gadgets gain advantage before Future pays off; Rug stops their Normal Summon trigger. Bringing it in together with Hero Blast requires removing Decree.

Matchup Side Plans

Gadgets / Monarch with small monsters
Side In: 2 x Hero Blast; 2 x Pulling the Rug
Side Out: 2 x Royal Decree; 1 x Future Fusion; 1 x Upstart Goblin
Switch from Decree to interaction: Blast recovers Sparkman and removes Gadgets, while Rug answers Monarch. Do not use Blast as an answer to a 2400 ATK Monarch. Keep one Future Fusion and the entire Poly and Miracle engine.

Dense backrow / Continuous Traps
Side In: 1 x Elemental HERO Wildheart; 2 x Spiritualism
Side Out: 1 x Mirror Force; 1 x Torrential Tribute; 1 x Ring of Destruction
The only traps left are the two Decrees. Wildheart is searchable and can attack despite opposing traps resolving; Spiritualism clears locks that are already active.

Gravekeeper / Necrovalley
Side In: 2 x Nobleman of Crossout; 2 x Spiritualism
Side Out: 1 x Premature Burial; 1 x Miracle Fusion; 1 x Future Fusion; 1 x Upstart Goblin
Keep one Miracle for after removing Necrovalley. Do not strip out Poly or E-Call. Decree can negate Oppression, but not Necrovalley; Spiritualism opens that window.

Fusions and graveyards: HERO / Dragon Future / Red-Eyes
Side In: 2 x De-Fusion; 2 x Soul Release
Side Out: 2 x Royal Decree; 1 x Upstart Goblin; 1 x Command Knight
Remove Decree against an opponent with few traps. Using De-Fusion on an opposing Fusion does not return materials from THEIR graveyard: the script requires the activating player's graveyard. Soul Release leaves your own Miracle materials untouched.

Effect-damage burn
Side In: 2 x Des Wombat; 1 x Elemental HERO Wildheart; 2 x Spiritualism
Side Out: 1 x Mirror Force; 1 x Torrential Tribute; 1 x Ring of Destruction; 1 x Upstart Goblin; 1 x Enemy Controller
Keep both Decrees and every Fusion route. Wombat protects against effect damage, not costs or battle damage. Do not add Hero Blast or Rug while retaining this Decree plan.

Chaos without a Fusion plan
Side In: 2 x Soul Release
Side Out: 1 x Future Fusion; 1 x Upstart Goblin
A small adjustment: remove their fuel without filling your Main Deck with monsters outside the HERO engine. There is no need to copy the four-card transformation used against Fusion decks.

title: Insect Normal
description:
Three Insect Knight and two Metal Armored Bug give value to Unexpected Dai, Summoner's Art, Ancient Rules, and Birthright. Recruiters and the Ultimate Insect chain offer alternative development.

NeoGoat Pro 0.3.2 beta.60 default deck | October 2026

PLAY GUIDE
Apply pressure with Normal Monsters, save ways to summon Metal Armored Bug, and evolve Ultimate Insect when you can protect it.

Game Plan
- Use Unexpected Dai on an empty field to summon Insect Knight, keeping your Normal Summon for a second monster or an answer.
- Search for Metal Armored Bug with Summoner's Art only when you have Ancient Rules, Pinch Hopper, or a later revival route.
- Evolve Ultimate Insect LV3 into LV5 and then LV7 during your Standby Phases; the Normal Monster plan keeps working while the chain develops.

Opening Turns
- Dai before your Normal Summon lets you open with Knight plus a recruiter. Check whether the second monster justifies exposing yourself to mass removal.
- A Set Howling Insect can find Pinch Hopper or Ultimate Insect LV3 after falling in battle; choose based on whether you have a large Insect in hand or time to evolve.

Key Plays and Synergies
- Ancient Rules summons Metal Armored Bug from the hand. Birthright brings Knight or Bug back from the GY to restore your attacking presence.
- Insect Imitation can Tribute a Level 4 monster to summon Ultimate Insect LV5; this produces a large monster through a different route from its natural evolution.
- Pinch Hopper sent from your field to the GY can summon an Insect from your hand, such as Metal Armored Bug, if its timing window is met.
- LV5 summoned by LV3's effect reduces opposing ATK; LV7 summoned by LV5 reduces ATK and DEF. Protect the transition to gain those benefits.

Common Mistakes
- The current list uses Nobleman of Crossout, not Foolish Burial. Do not assume you have a direct GY send that is no longer in the Main Deck.
- Pinch Hopper has an optional 'when' effect: it can miss timing if its trip to the GY is not the last thing to happen, such as when Tributed as a cost.
- LV5 summoned by Insect Imitation does not gain the ATK reduction associated with being summoned by LV3; the same applies to LV7 if it did not arrive through LV5.
- Unexpected Dai requires an empty field and only summons a Level 4 or lower Normal Monster; Summoner's Art searches for Level 5 or higher Normal Monsters, so it cannot find Knight.

SIDE DECK GUIDE
Each plan starts from the original deck list and swaps an equal number of cards in and out. Choose a plan based on what you saw in Game 1; do not combine complete plans. These are practice guidelines with verified card counts and legality, not claims of proven performance in human matches.

Side Card Roles
- 2 x Order to Charge: With five actual Normal Monsters and Dai/Birthright, it turns a threatened Normal Monster into non-targeting destruction of an opposing monster. The Tribute happens on resolution, so your Normal Monster must still be valid; it cannot Tribute Pinch Hopper or Tokens.
- 1 x Dust Barrier: Temporarily protects the five Normal Monsters from the opponent's Smashing/Brain/Soul Exchange/Book without making them immune to your own Spells as Non-Spellcasting Area would. It does not protect Ultimate or other Effect Monsters, and it destroys itself during your second Standby Phase.
- 1 x Swarm of Locusts: A Howling search target for slow games against Traps and Continuous cards. It destroys on a Flip SUMMON, not when flipped by an attack; it needs to survive and get a genuine opportunity.
- 1 x Swarm of Scarabs: A second, different Howling target for repeatable advantage against slow monster strategies. Do not bring it in against aggro that will not let you Flip Summon.
- 2 x 4-Starred Ladybug of Doom: Two FLIP answers to multiple opposing face-up Level 4 monsters, such as Warriors, Amazoness or Gadgets. Howling Insect can summon it face-up, but that does not activate its FLIP effect: normally Set it from hand. It is not a substitute for GY hate and does not destroy monsters of other Levels.
- 2 x Nobleman of Crossout: Against Spy/FLIP monsters, clears a path for Insect Knight and Metal Armored Bug. The Swarms are not FLIP monsters and do not activate simply by being flipped face-up.
- 2 x Seven Tools of the Bandit: Negates the activation of Mirror/Torrential/Bottomless/Oppression without shutting off Birthright and Call. Costs 1000 LP; it does not negate an effect of an Oppression that was already active.
- 2 x Pulling the Rug: Negates Monarch/Gadget effects on Normal Summon, preserving your large bodies and revival support.
- 2 x Des Wombat: Against Burn/Solar Flare, replaces ineffective LP pressure with continuous protection from effect damage. Neither Howling nor Rat can summon it (1600 ATK).

Matchup Side Plans

Warrior / Amazoness / Level 4 monster pressure
Side In: 2 x 4-Starred Ladybug of Doom; 2 x Order to Charge
Side Out: 1 x Ultimate Insect LV7; 1 x Ultimate Insect LV5; 1 x Ultimate Insect LV3; 1 x Insect Imitation
Shifts to immediate answers by removing the entire LV line. Keeps all five Normal Monsters, Unexpected Dai, Birthright and Pinch Hopper. Set Ladybug to use its FLIP effect; Order to Charge trades a Normal Monster for an opposing monster. This plan does not banish cards from the GY.

Monarch / Gadgets
Side In: 2 x Pulling the Rug; 2 x Order to Charge; 1 x Dust Barrier
Side Out: 1 x Ancient Rules; 1 x Summoner's Art; 1 x Pinch Hopper; 1 x Lightning Vortex; 1 x Nobleman of Crossout
Keeps all five Normal Monsters, one Art, one Pinch and the complete LV line. Dust Barrier protects Normal Monsters from opposing Spells, not Zaborg: Rug answers that trigger. Remove the Main Deck Nobleman if you have not seen relevant FLIP defenders.

Slow Trap control
Side In: 1 x Swarm of Locusts; 2 x Seven Tools of the Bandit
Side Out: 1 x Ancient Rules; 1 x Metal Armored Bug; 1 x Summoner's Art
Keeps one Metal with one Art, both Pinches and all three Knights. Locust is a Howling toolbox option, not a promise of immediate destruction after being attacked.

Slow monster control / Wall Rock
Side In: 1 x Swarm of Scarabs; 2 x Nobleman of Crossout
Side Out: 1 x Ancient Rules; 1 x Summoner's Art; 1 x Lightning Vortex
Scarabs only needs a Flip Summon and can destroy even defenders you would rather not battle. Against faster control, omit Scarabs from this plan and swap only the two Crossouts. Keep the Main Deck Nobleman for three Crossouts in total. Vortex comes out because it is less precise against Set defenders.

Gravekeeper with Necrovalley and Traps
Side In: 2 x Nobleman of Crossout; 1 x Swarm of Locusts; 2 x Seven Tools of the Bandit
Side Out: 1 x Premature Burial; 1 x Call of the Haunted; 2 x Birthright; 1 x Ancient Rules
Do not rely on revival under Necrovalley. Locust offers another way to remove the Field Spell alongside Heavy/MST/Breaker/Dust/Gigantes. Seven Tools must answer a Trap's ACTIVATION, not an already active Oppression. Ancient Rules comes out with all four revival cards; keep all three Noblemen for Spy/Guard.

Burn / Solar Flare
Side In: 2 x Des Wombat; 1 x Swarm of Locusts; 2 x Seven Tools of the Bandit
Side Out: 1 x Mirror Force; 1 x Torrential Tribute; 1 x Ring of Destruction; 1 x Premature Burial; 1 x Injection Fairy Lily
Removes your own LP payments/self-damage and less useful battle responses. Seven Tools costs LP: negate the relevant piece rather than spending it indiscriminately. If the opponent is playing Pyro aggro rather than burn, do not automatically make all five swaps.

title: Mazera DeVille
description:
Three Warrior of Zera, two Unexpected Dai, and Reinforcement of the Army prepare Mazera's Tribute. General finds Pandemonium, while three Dark Spirit's Mastery access the two Mazera DeVille or Dark Necrofear.

NeoGoat Pro 0.3.2 beta.60 default deck | October 2026

PLAY GUIDE
Assemble Zera, Pandemonium, and Mazera without spending your entire hand, and force the three-card discard while the opponent still has resources.

Game Plan
- Identify the missing piece before searching: Zera, Pandemonium, or Mazera. Avoid spending several searchers on copies of something already available.
- Apply pressure with Archfiend Soldier, Mist Archfiend, and Newdoria while preparing the combo; you do not need to leave your field empty while waiting for the perfect hand.
- With three Fiends in the GY, Dark Necrofear offers another threat. Preserve the Mazera route if the opponent still has a valuable hand.

Opening Turns
- On an empty field, Unexpected Dai summons Warrior of Zera. General can search for Pandemonium, and Dark Spirit's Mastery finds Mazera for a discard.
- If several pieces are missing, use Newdoria or a Fiend attacker and Set protection; save Dai for a turn when your field can be empty.

Key Plays and Synergies
- Mazera summons itself from the hand by Tributing a face-up Warrior of Zera with Pandemonium on the field; to force the three-card discard, Pandemonium must be on your side.
- Dark Spirit's Mastery searches for or recovers a Level 8 Fiend: both Mazera and Dark Necrofear meet that requirement.
- Mist Archfiend summoned without a Tribute can attack and destroy itself in the End Phase; Pandemonium turns that destruction into a lower-Level Archfiend.
- Tribe-Infecting Virus and Mastery's discards can prepare Fiends for Dark Necrofear; count three usable monsters before committing to it.

Common Mistakes
- There is no Chaos Sorcerer in this list: you do not need to preserve LIGHT/DARK monsters for a nonexistent Chaos engine.
- Mazera cannot be revived with Call of the Haunted or Premature Burial, nor simply Tribute Summoned. It requires its own procedure.
- An opposing Pandemonium satisfies the Summoning condition but not Mazera's discard effect; losing your own Field Spell before resolution also matters.
- Card Destruction can refill a hand that Mazera just emptied. Mist deals 1000 damage even while you control Pandemonium.

SIDE DECK GUIDE
Each plan starts from the original deck list and swaps an equal number of cards in and out. Choose a plan based on what you saw in Game 1; do not combine complete plans. These are practice guidelines with verified card counts and legality, not claims of proven performance in human matches.

Side Card Roles
- 2 x Falling Down: With Soldier, General or Mist face-up, equips to and takes control of an opposing monster while it remains equipped, opening Mazera's attack without sacrificing Warrior of Zera. It inflicts 800 damage to you during each opponent's Standby Phase, and Pandemonium does not prevent it.
- 2 x Gemini Imps: Defends combo pieces against the opponent's discard effects, draws a card and also supplies DARK/Fiend fuel for Dark Necrofear when used.
- 2 x Pulling the Rug: A tempo answer to Monarchs, Gadgets and Breaker without committing Warrior of Zera.
- 2 x Bottomless Trap Hole: Banishes Monarchs and Fusion/Chaos bosses. The Main Deck has no copies, so two can come in without exceeding the limit.
- 2 x Dust Tornado: Removes Necrovalley, Village, Hunting Ground, Royal Oppression and backrow before the combo turn.
- 1 x Spiritualism: Its activation and effect cannot be negated; temporarily removes a face-up floodgate or backrow card during the decisive turn.
- 2 x Soul Release: Removes Chaos, Zombie and GY Fusion materials at once by targeting only the opponent's GY.
- 2 x My Body as a Shield: Protects Warrior of Zera or Mazera from Torrential, Bottomless, Vortex and monster destruction during the critical window.

Matchup Side Plans

Monarch / Gadget
Side In: 2 x Gemini Imps; 2 x Pulling the Rug; 2 x Bottomless Trap Hole
Side Out: 1 x Dark Necrofear; 2 x Mist Archfiend; 2 x Newdoria; 1 x Card Destruction
Rug and Bottomless cover the summon; Gemini Imps stops Thestalos from breaking up your combo hand, and removing Card Destruction avoids refilling the Gadget player's hand.

Chaos / Zombie / Red-Eyes / HERO
Side In: 2 x Soul Release; 2 x Dust Tornado
Side Out: 1 x Dark Necrofear; 2 x Mist Archfiend; 1 x Newdoria
Soul Release removes materials only from the opponent's GY, while Dust cuts off Continuous cards and revival. Necrofear comes out because it is slow and requires its own setup, not because Soul Release affects your GY.

Gravekeeper / Field Spell floodgates
Side In: 2 x Dust Tornado; 1 x Spiritualism; 2 x My Body as a Shield
Side Out: 2 x Newdoria; 2 x Mist Archfiend; 1 x Dark Necrofear
Three Spell/Trap answers clear Necrovalley or Oppression, while My Body protects Zera/Mazera from the destructive response.

Amazoness / Earth Aggro / Armed Dragon
Side In: 2 x Falling Down; 2 x Bottomless Trap Hole; 2 x My Body as a Shield
Side Out: 2 x Mist Archfiend; 2 x Newdoria; 1 x Dark Necrofear; 1 x Card Destruction
Keep Soldier/General to support Falling Down; Bottomless handles large bodies, and My Body protects your push.

Thestalos / Spirit Reaper / hand discard
Side In: 2 x Gemini Imps
Side Out: 2 x Newdoria
Gemini Imps comes in only when you have seen discard caused by an opponent's effect; it is not meant to answer discards paid as costs.
