title: Monarch
description:
Nine Gadgets chain searches and provide bodies for seven Monarchs. Two Soul Exchange and Brain Control turn opposing monsters into Tributes while removal keeps attacks open.

NeoGoat Pro 0.3.2 beta.60 default deck | October 2026

PLAY GUIDE
Maintain the Gadget chain, turn a small monster into a useful Monarch, and keep the initiative with efficient removal.

Game Plan
- Summon a Gadget and search for the next color still in the Deck; preserve the chain to produce monsters across several turns.
- Choose the Monarch for its effect: Zaborg against monsters, Mobius against backrow, and Thestalos against a hand worth reducing.
- Use Soul Exchange when giving up the Battle Phase is worth removing a threat and developing a Monarch; Brain Control supports a different kind of offensive turn.

Opening Turns
- A Gadget plus Sakuretsu Armor or Shrink creates a modest field that replaces itself in hand and can survive to become Tribute material later.
- If the opponent already presents a threat, Soul Exchange plus a Monarch can turn the field around without consuming your own Gadget.

Key Plays and Synergies
- After a Gadget has searched, Tribute it on a later turn to convert its body into a Monarch effect.
- Gigantes and The Rock Spirit banish a used EARTH monster from the GY to provide another attacker or Tribute without consuming your Normal Summon.
- Mobius can remove up to two Spells/Traps; choose the cards that obstruct your attack plan, accounting for Set cards that can be chained.
- Swords of Revealing Light buys time for a hand containing Monarchs; Gadgets and removal help turn those extra turns into resources.

Common Mistakes
- Soul Exchange prevents your Battle Phase that turn. Do not calculate a finish through attacks after activating it.
- Zaborg must destroy a monster when resolving; if there is no other valid target, it can end up destroying itself.
- Do not control more Gadgets than necessary against Torrential Tribute or Mirror Force; part of their advantage lies in your next Summon.
- Gigantes destroyed by battle wipes out your own backrow. The seven Monarchs can clog your hand if you spend all your monsters without preserving Tribute material.

SIDE DECK GUIDE
Each plan starts from the original deck list and swaps an equal number of cards in and out. Choose a plan based on what you saw in Game 1; do not combine complete plans. These are practice guidelines with verified card counts and legality, not claims of proven performance in human matches.

Side Card Roles
- 2 x Banisher of the Radiance: A consistent anti-GY transformation: Gigantes and Rock Spirit come out. This Main Deck has no revival cards; all nine Gadgets still search on the field. Two anti-GY bodies, not three that would overcrowd your Normal Summons.
- 1 x The End of Anubis: A 2500 ATK Tribute monster that negates effects activated in the GY or targeting it, including Gozuki's GY effect and targeted revival; it does not stop Gozuki from sending cards from the Deck. Replaces a Monarch rather than adding another Tribute monster. It does not negate Miracle/Dragon's Mirror, which banish without targeting.
- 2 x Mind Crush: Disrupts cards known from public Gadget, Manju or E - Emergency Call searches. Both you and your opponent must have at least one card in hand to activate it. Two copies attack hand redundancy without discarding from your own hand unless you miss; do not name cards blindly or discard Despair from the Dark.
- 2 x Pulling the Rug: A direct answer in the Gadget/Monarch mirror. Two copies leave room for other matchups and do not require the monster to remain vulnerable to battle destruction.
- 2 x Cipher Soldier: Against Warriors/Amazoness, provides a low-Level body that both attacks and defends to support Tributes. Gadgets do not search it, and the deck does not have Rat.
- 2 x Des Wombat: Two anti-burn bodies that can still apply pressure; trim less useful Tribute monsters and removal to avoid losing to a clogged hand.
- 1 x Dust Tornado: The third copy overall, to cut off an opponent's response or remove an active Continuous card. One copy here because the deck already has two Mobius, Heavy and MST.
- 1 x Nobleman of Crossout: An answer to Set defenders/FLIP monsters that avoids giving away battle advantage. One copy alongside the Main Deck's three Smashings, since they cover different battle positions.
- 2 x Seven Tools of the Bandit: Protects the investment in a Tribute Summon from Solemn/other Traps and enables a decisive attack. Two copies without shutting off your own eight-Trap package; each use costs 1000 LP.

Matchup Side Plans

Zombie / GY and revival
Side In: 2 x Banisher of the Radiance; 1 x The End of Anubis
Side Out: 1 x Gigantes; 1 x The Rock Spirit; 1 x Thestalos the Firestorm Monarch
3 in, 3 out. Removes both of your own banishing costs so you do not depend on a GY that Banisher empties. Keeps nine Gadgets and seven Tribute monsters by replacing Thestalos with Anubis. Anubis is not a universal negator of Fusions that banish materials.

Warrior / Amazoness
Side In: 2 x Cipher Soldier; 1 x Nobleman of Crossout
Side Out: 2 x Thestalos the Firestorm Monarch; 1 x Soul Exchange
3 in, 3 out. Drops from seven to five Tribute monsters for faster defense while keeping nine Gadgets. Crossout removes only Set monsters; Cipher holds the board for your remaining Tribute monsters.

Gadget Monarch mirror
Side In: 2 x Pulling the Rug; 2 x Mind Crush
Side Out: 1 x Soul Exchange; 1 x Swords of Revealing Light; 2 x Shrink
4 in, 4 out. Rug stops the Normal Summon from generating value. Use Mind Crush after seeing the card added by Gadget and before it leaves the opponent's hand, keeping at least one card in your own hand so you can activate it. Keeps all nine Gadgets and seven Monarchs.

Burn / stall
Side In: 2 x Des Wombat; 1 x Dust Tornado; 2 x Seven Tools of the Bandit
Side Out: 2 x Zaborg the Thunder Monarch; 2 x Soul Exchange; 1 x Brain Control
5 in, 5 out. Keeps both Mobius for backrow, drops to five Tribute monsters and avoids dead control-taking/Tribute Spells. Wombat establishes protection, while Dust removes Continuous cards; spend LP on Tools only to establish or preserve that protection.

Search-heavy HERO / Ritual with Traps
Side In: 2 x Mind Crush; 1 x Dust Tornado; 2 x Seven Tools of the Bandit
Side Out: 2 x Soul Exchange; 1 x Swords of Revealing Light; 1 x Smashing Ground; 1 x Thestalos the Firestorm Monarch
5 in, 5 out. Mind Crush requires a card in your own hand and information from E - Emergency Call, Manju or a Polymerization search, not a guess. Tools protects Tribute monsters from Trap activations, not effects of already face-up Traps; Dust retains an answer to Future/Continuous cards. Six Tribute monsters, nine Gadgets and monster removal remain. Do not use this discard against Despair when it would benefit from being sent by the opponent.

title: Pyro Fire

Three Bonfire find small Pyros, and three UFO Turtle sustain development. Solar Flare Dragon, Volcanic Slicer, and the Inpachi package combine effect damage with attacks.

NeoGoat Pro 0.3.2 beta.60 default deck | October 2026

PLAY GUIDE
Find the right Pyro, alternate pressure and effect damage, and preserve FIRE monsters for Spirit of Flames and Oil.

Game Plan
- Use Bonfire to complete the position you actually need: Solar Flare for sustained damage, Slicer for a finish, or a useful Pyro body.
- Maintain the field with UFO Turtle and Inpachi before committing Thestalos. Unexpected Dai must resolve while you still control no monsters.
- Count End Phase damage before attacking with everything; several Solar Flare can finish without exposing every monster to a battle Trap.

Opening Turns
- Dai summons Blazing Inpachi for pressure or Charcoal Inpachi for defense; you can then use your Normal Summon for another Pyro.
- A Set UFO Turtle can recruit a FIRE monster with 1500 ATK or less, such as Solar Flare, when destroyed by battle.

Key Plays and Synergies
- Two Solar Flare Dragon protect each other from attacks because each has another Pyro alongside it; each deals 500 damage in your End Phase if its effect resolves.
- Volcanic Slicer can deal 500 instead of attacking that turn. Compare that guaranteed amount with the battle damage available.
- Spirit of Flames banishes a FIRE monster from the GY to summon itself and gains 300 ATK in your Battle Phase, expanding your offense without using the Normal Summon.
- Oil recovers up to two Level 4 or lower FIRE monsters with different names; choose useful monsters for next turn or discards for Raigeki Break.

Common Mistakes
- Bonfire searches for Level 4 or lower Pyros, not any FIRE monster: it cannot find UFO Turtle, Tenkabito Shien, or Thestalos.
- Solar Flare Dragon is a Pyro despite its name. Its protection does not stop destruction, banishing, or effects that return it to the hand.
- Spirit of Flames can consume the target you needed for Oil or revival. Oil cannot recover Thestalos because of its Level.
- Gaia Soul the Combustible Collective destroys itself in the End Phase; use it for an immediate gain. Molten Destruction also boosts the opponent's FIRE monsters.

SIDE DECK GUIDE
Each plan starts from the original deck list and swaps an equal number of cards in and out. Choose a plan based on what you saw in Game 1; do not combine complete plans. These are practice guidelines with verified card counts and legality, not claims of proven performance in human matches.

Side Card Roles
- 2 x Des Wombat: Wins the burn mirror by reducing damage from Solar Flare, Volcanic Slicer and Traps to zero while still providing 1600 ATK.
- 2 x Dust Tornado: Chainable removal for Field Spells, Future Fusion, Call and floodgates while keeping your own Traps active.
- 2 x Pulling the Rug: A clean trade against Monarchs, Gadgets and Breaker.
- 2 x Mask of Restrict: Shuts down opposing Tribute Summons; the plan removes both of your own Thestalos copies.
- 2 x Kycoo the Ghost Destroyer: Prevents the opponent from banishing cards from the GYs for Chaos or Fusions without stopping its controller from banishing FIRE monsters from their own GY for Spirit of Flames. Does not stop materials from being banished from the field.

title: Red-Eyes
description:
Three Manju and two Paladin of Dark Dragon connect the Ritual engine to three Red-Eyes B. Dragon. Future Fusion, Red-Eyes Wyvern, and two Red-Eyes Spirit provide setup and revival, with Metamorphosis as an Extra Deck option.

NeoGoat Pro 0.3.2 beta.60 default deck | October 2026

PLAY GUIDE
Choose between a Ritual opening and Future Fusion's delayed plan; preserve Wyvern's conditions to bring back Red-Eyes.

Game Plan
- Use Manju to find the missing Ritual half. Ragged Records of Rites can find Paladin by revealing Dark Dragon Ritual from your hand or Deck.
- Load Red-Eyes and Wyvern when you have revival or can set aside a turn without a Normal Summon/Set; do not send materials without checking the follow-up.
- Use large monsters to force answers before Dragon's Mirror or Metamorphosis, choosing a Fusion that can change the field.

Opening Turns
- Manju plus one Ritual piece completes access to Paladin. Advanced Ritual Art can send a Level 4 Luster Dragon from the Deck to Ritual Summon it.
- Future Fusion with protection prepares Five-Headed Dragon: in the first subsequent Standby Phase it sends five Dragons, including Red-Eyes or Wyvern depending on your hand.

Key Plays and Synergies
- At the start of the Damage Step, Paladin destroys the Defense Position monster it attacks; afterward you can Tribute Paladin to summon an eligible Red-Eyes from your hand or Deck.
- On a later turn than the one it was sent to the GY, Dark Dragon Ritual can banish itself to search for Red-Eyes Spirit.
- Red-Eyes Wyvern banishes itself to revive an eligible Red-Eyes in your End Phase, provided you did not Normal Summon or Set during that turn.
- Metamorphosis turns Level 7 Red-Eyes B. Dragon into an available Level 7 Fusion, such as King Dragun; consider the consequences of choosing The Last Warrior from Another Planet.

Common Mistakes
- Normal Summoning or Setting disables Wyvern that turn, even if that monster later leaves the field.
- Future Fusion sends nothing on activation. Do not plan an immediate Red-Eyes Spirit using materials that are still in the Deck.
- Red-Eyes Darkness Dragon requires Tributing Red-Eyes B. Dragon and is not an ordinary revival target; Paladin does not ignore Summoning conditions either.
- The Last Warrior from Another Planet destroys your other monsters and blocks further Summons; do not choose it if you need to keep developing.

SIDE DECK GUIDE
Each plan starts from the original deck list and swaps an equal number of cards in and out. Choose a plan based on what you saw in Game 1; do not combine complete plans. These are practice guidelines with verified card counts and legality, not claims of proven performance in human matches.

Side Card Roles
- 2 x Stamping Destruction: A Dragon is frequently on the field, making this a Spell-based answer to Necrovalley/Oppression/Drain without disabling Red-Eyes Spirit. Paladin is a Dragon; Manju is not.
- 1 x Giant Trunade: Opens a window for Ritual Summons, revival or attacks against backrow. It also returns your own Continuous and Equip cards: activate it before investing in Future or after getting value from it, not as a free board clear.
- 2 x Soul Release: Removes the opponent's GY without blocking your own Wyvern/Spirit/Mirror. Banisher is not added to solve one matchup at the cost of creating another internal conflict.
- 2 x Compulsory Evacuation Device: An answer to Chaos, Ritual and Fusion monsters that does not rely on winning battles or destroying them. Do not use it indiscriminately against Manju/Gadgets that would search again.
- 2 x Mind Crush: Against search engines, remove the piece after seeing what Manju/Ragged/E-Call/Gadget searched. You need a card in your own hand and should not guess blindly; discarding an opposing Red-Eyes can help the opponent if you choose the wrong piece.
- 2 x Des Wombat: Protection against burn while the Future/Ritual route develops. It does not depend on the GY or Traps, and creates no Totem conflict because this Main Deck does not use Totem.
- 2 x Pulling the Rug: Against Monarchs/Gadgets/Manju, negates the effect on Normal Summon and destroys its source. An alternative to Mind Crush's discard depending on your hand and the turn.
- 2 x Nobleman of Crossout: Removes Spy/Guard and other FLIP monsters blocking Red-Eyes. Complements Paladin without first requiring a Ritual Summon and an attack.

Matchup Side Plans

Gravekeeper with Necrovalley
Side In: 2 x Stamping Destruction; 1 x Giant Trunade; 2 x Nobleman of Crossout
Side Out: 2 x Red-Eyes Spirit; 1 x Premature Burial; 1 x Call of the Haunted; 1 x Foolish Burial
Removes five GY-dependent cards while keeping the Ritual routes from hand/Deck. The remaining Wyvern and Mirror need Necrovalley removed to be useful.

Chaos / Zombie
Side In: 2 x Soul Release; 2 x Compulsory Evacuation Device
Side Out: 1 x Red-Eyes Darkness Dragon; 1 x Future Fusion; 1 x Metamorphosis; 1 x Dark Dragon Ritual
One Future, one Dark Dragon Ritual, ARA, Ragged and three Manjus remain: the engine stays intact with a lower ceiling and fewer slow-tempo cards. Compulsory can remove Chaos in response to its effect, but does not negate it; an already activated effect still resolves if its target remains valid.

Gadget Monarch
Side In: 2 x Pulling the Rug; 2 x Mind Crush
Side Out: 1 x Red-Eyes Darkness Dragon; 1 x Future Fusion; 1 x Metamorphosis; 1 x Dark Dragon Ritual
Use Mind Crush on the Gadget actually added to the hand or otherwise known; do not assume you know a hidden Monarch. Rug negates the Normal Summon trigger. Do not spend both cards on the same search that Rug already negated.

Trap-heavy decks / established locks
Side In: 2 x Stamping Destruction; 1 x Giant Trunade
Side Out: 1 x Red-Eyes Darkness Dragon; 1 x Future Fusion; 1 x Dark Dragon Ritual
Keeps both Spirits and Call, which is why Decree is not added. Stamping requires a face-up Dragon and can use Paladin/Luster/Masked/Red-Eyes.

Effect-damage burn
Side In: 2 x Des Wombat; 2 x Stamping Destruction; 1 x Giant Trunade
Side Out: 1 x Mirror Force; 1 x Torrential Tribute; 1 x Ring of Destruction; 1 x Red-Eyes Darkness Dragon; 1 x Metamorphosis
Keeps the Ritual engine and Red-Eyes recursion. Wombat buys the time Future needs; the Spells remove attack barriers and continuous damage sources.

HERO / Ritual / Red-Eyes with revealed searches
Side In: 2 x Soul Release; 2 x Compulsory Evacuation Device; 2 x Mind Crush
Side Out: 1 x Mirror Force; 1 x Torrential Tribute; 1 x Ring of Destruction; 1 x Red-Eyes Darkness Dragon; 1 x Metamorphosis; 1 x Future Fusion
Trades battle-based removal for interaction with engine pieces and the GY. Use Mind Crush on a searched Ritual/Fusion Spell; avoid discarding fuel that gives the opponent an advantage. Compulsory returns Fusion Monsters to the Extra Deck.

title: Relinquished

description:
Three Relinquished, five Ritual searchers, and four Ritual Spells support the absorption plan. Two D.D. Trainer supply Advanced Ritual Art, while six LIGHT monsters enable a second route with Chaos Sorcerer.

NeoGoat Pro 0.3.2 beta.60 default deck | October 2026

PLAY GUIDE
Complete the Ritual with as few resources as possible, absorb a useful threat, and manage Relinquished's equipped monster.

Game Plan
- Use Manju, Senju, or Sonic Bird to find the missing piece, checking your materials before searching for redundant copies.
- Summon Relinquished when there is a target worth the investment; removing a monster by equipping it can answer threats you would rather not destroy.
- Keep LIGHT and DARK monsters in the GY for the two Chaos Sorcerer, but do not spend your Ritual route just to accelerate that secondary plan.

Opening Turns
- Advanced Ritual Art sends a Level 1 D.D. Trainer from the Deck to summon Relinquished; check that one remains there.
- Ragged Records of Rites can reveal Black Illusion Ritual in the hand or Deck to search for Relinquished, then Manju finds the missing Spell.

Key Plays and Synergies
- Relinquished absorbs an opposing monster as an Equip Card and copies its stats; choose a useful attacker or a threat that must be removed.
- On a later turn, Tsukuyomi or Book of Moon can Set Relinquished and remove its equipped card. If it can legally be flipped again, another absorption becomes available.
- Raigeki Break can destroy the equipped card when freeing Relinquished to absorb another threat is worth the discard.
- Apprentice Magician can prepare Old Vindictive Magician; that line offers interaction while you assemble the Ritual pieces.

Common Mistakes
- Relinquished can only hold one monster equipped through its effect; it cannot absorb another while keeping the previous one.
- Absorbing a Set monster does not guarantee that its printed ATK will become useful attacking power. Check the result before planning damage.
- An equipped card does not make Relinquished immune to effects, and you still take the battle damage that its text also inflicts on the opponent.
- Advanced Ritual Art needs exact Levels from the Deck: with both D.D. Trainer in the hand or GY, that route has no material. Chaos also cannot attack if it uses its banishing effect.

SIDE DECK GUIDE
Each plan starts from the original deck list and swaps an equal number of cards in and out. Choose a plan based on what you saw in Game 1; do not combine complete plans. These are practice guidelines with verified card counts and legality, not claims of proven performance in human matches.

Side Card Roles
- 2 x Kycoo the Ghost Destroyer: DARK pressure against Chaos/Zombie without banishing your own pieces. Your Kycoo prevents the OPPONENT from banishing from the GYs, not your own Chaos summons.
- 2 x Cursed Seal of the Forbidden Spell: Against a repeated engine Spell (Future/Miracle/Ritual) or a Field Spell that has not resolved yet, a redundant Spell pays to negate, destroy and lock out the opponent's future copies. Do not use it if you must discard your only Ritual route.
- 2 x Seven Tools of the Bandit: Protects Ritual Summons and absorption against Trap activations without disabling Raigeki Break or Call. Costs 1000 LP and does not answer the effect of an already active Continuous Trap.
- 2 x Compulsory Evacuation Device: Against Fusion/Ritual/Chaos monsters or a monster you cannot absorb. A non-destruction answer; returning your own Relinquished requires another Ritual Summon, so it is not a free reset.
- 2 x Divine Wrath: Negates Chaos/Monarch/Harpie effects and protects Relinquished from removal by monster effects. Sinister can pay the cost, but the card still requires a discard.
- 2 x Des Wombat: Against burn while Relinquished limits attacks. Both Chaos copies come out in this plan so you do not need to support another engine alongside Ritual.
- 1 x Giant Trunade: Temporarily removes Necrovalley/Oppression/Drain and opens absorption/Ritual plays. It also returns cards equipped to Relinquished to their owners' hands; evaluate that before activating it.
- 2 x Nobleman of Crossout: Removes Spy/Guard/FLIP monsters without absorbing a low-ATK monster. Against an opposing Old Vindictive, it can banish yours from the Deck; keeping Tsukuyomi and Apprentice does not remove that caveat.

Matchup Side Plans

Chaos / Zombie
Side In: 2 x Kycoo the Ghost Destroyer; 2 x Divine Wrath
Side Out: 2 x Apprentice Magician; 1 x Old Vindictive Magician; 1 x Ragged Records of Rites
Removes the entire three-Spellcaster slow recruiter package. Keeps all six LIGHT monsters and five Ritual searchers. Kycoo only removes GY cards when it deals damage, and its banishing restriction applies only to the opponent.

Fusion / Ritual using repeated Spells
Side In: 2 x Cursed Seal of the Forbidden Spell; 2 x Compulsory Evacuation Device
Side Out: 2 x Apprentice Magician; 1 x Old Vindictive Magician; 1 x Raigeki Break
Removes the slow Flip package, not part of the Ritual engine. Cursed Seal requires a Spell discard and successful destruction to apply its lasting lock. Compulsory returns Fusion Monsters to the Extra Deck; it does not negate already activated effects.

Monarch with monster removal
Side In: 2 x Divine Wrath; 2 x Compulsory Evacuation Device
Side Out: 2 x Apprentice Magician; 1 x Old Vindictive Magician; 1 x Ragged Records of Rites
Wrath negates the effect when it activates; Compulsory does not, so save it for another threat or to remove an attacker. Avoid routinely returning Gadgets. Do not combine this plan with another that removes the same three monsters.

Heavy backrow / Traps
Side In: 2 x Seven Tools of the Bandit; 1 x Giant Trunade
Side Out: 1 x Mirror Force; 1 x Torrential Tribute; 1 x Ring of Destruction
Keeps Raigeki Break for interaction and keeps Call. Seven Tools answers activations; use Heavy/MST/Breaker/Trunade for an already active Continuous card. Trunade can return the monster equipped to Relinquished to the opponent's hand.

Gravekeeper / Necrovalley
Side In: 2 x Nobleman of Crossout; 1 x Giant Trunade; 2 x Seven Tools of the Bandit
Side Out: 2 x Chaos Sorcerer; 1 x Premature Burial; 1 x Call of the Haunted; 1 x Advanced Ritual Art
Three Relinquished, two Black Illusions, one ARA, two Raggeds and all searchers remain. Abandons Chaos under Necrovalley; Relinquished does not depend on the GY to absorb monsters. Seven Tools removes neither Necrovalley nor an already face-up Oppression.

Effect-damage burn
Side In: 2 x Des Wombat; 1 x Giant Trunade; 2 x Seven Tools of the Bandit
Side Out: 2 x Chaos Sorcerer; 1 x Mirror Force; 1 x Torrential Tribute; 1 x Ring of Destruction
A pure Ritual plan: Wombat covers effect damage, and Relinquished applies pressure without taking Ring's self-damaging trade. Save the LP payment for Seven Tools for an important piece.

title: Spellcaster
description:
Three Apprentice Magician, Spy, and several Flip Effects maintain resources for Magical Dimension. Two Chaos Sorcerer, Chaos Command Magician, and Dark Magician of Chaos offer different ways to turn that development into pressure.

NeoGoat Pro 0.3.2 beta.60 default deck | October 2026

PLAY GUIDE
Buy time with small Spellcasters, preserve your LIGHT monsters, and choose the moment to turn a body into a boss.

Game Plan
- Use Apprentice to access Crystal Seer or Old Vindictive Magician depending on whether you need to find cards or remove a monster.
- Keep the list's six LIGHT monsters available as resources for Chaos; do not confuse the Spellcaster Type with the DARK Attribute.
- Save Magical Dimension for a threat in hand and a situation where Tributing your monster and destroying another creates a clear improvement.

Opening Turns
- A Set Apprentice or Spy plus protection lets you develop without committing a high-Level boss.
- With a face-up Spellcaster, Magical Dimension, and Dark Magician of Chaos in hand, prepare the replacement when the opponent tries to remove your monster or when you can benefit from the destruction.

Key Plays and Synergies
- Magical Dimension requires you to control a Spellcaster, Tributes your chosen monster, and summons a Spellcaster from your hand; afterward it can destroy a monster.
- Dark Magician of Chaos recovers a Spell in the End Phase of the turn it was Summoned; protect its presence and choose the resource that makes your next turn useful.
- Tsukuyomi Sets Spy, Guard, or a useful Flip monster again for later reuse.
- Apprentice can place a counter on Breaker when it is a valid target, giving Breaker another way to remove backrow.

Common Mistakes
- Dark Magician of Chaos does not recover a Spell immediately on Summon. If it leaves the field face-up, it is banished.
- Magical Dimension needs a Spellcaster to activate and another summonable one in hand; it is not standalone removal with an empty hand.
- Skilled Blue Magician supplies LIGHT and defense, but this list has no targets for its Summoning effect. Banishing it from the GY to place a counter also consumes a LIGHT monster that Chaos may need.
- Chaos Command Magician does not protect your whole field: it negates monster effects that target only itself. Necrovalley and an opposing Kycoo can stop the Chaos plan.

SIDE DECK GUIDE
Each plan starts from the original deck list and swaps an equal number of cards in and out. Choose a plan based on what you saw in Game 1; do not combine complete plans. These are practice guidelines with verified card counts and legality, not claims of proven performance in human matches.

Side Card Roles
- 2 x Dark Renewal: Uses any face-up Spellcaster to remove an opposing summon and converts the trade into Dark Magician of Chaos or another DARK Spellcaster from the Deck/GY.
- 2 x Kycoo the Ghost Destroyer: Completes the three legal copies alongside the Main Deck copy. A DARK Spellcaster with 1800 ATK that prevents the opponent from banishing cards from the GYs for Chaos, Miracle Fusion or Dragon's Mirror. Those two Fusion Spells can still use field materials.
- 2 x Dust Tornado: Removes Field Spells and floodgates without Raigeki Break's discard and lets you Set a control Trap.
- 2 x Pulling the Rug: Negates Monarch, Gadget and Breaker effects in their Normal Summon window.
- 2 x Mind Crush: Punishes confirmed information from Gadget, Commandant, Harpie Queen, E - Emergency Call and Reinforcement of the Army.
- 2 x Nobleman of Crossout: Alongside the Main Deck copy, reaches three against Spy, Apprentice and Wall without exposing a Spellcaster to combat.
- 2 x Divine Wrath: A universal answer to monster effects; discarding LIGHT/DARK monsters prepares Chaos Sorcerer and revival plays.
- 1 x Cursed Seal of the Forbidden Spell: The high Spell count supports its cost and prevents further activations of the same name for the rest of the Duel, such as Future Fusion, Miracle Fusion, Book of Life or Dark Spirit's Mastery. The restriction does not carry over to other Duels in the Match.

Matchup Side Plans

Monarch / Gadget
Side In: 2 x Pulling the Rug; 2 x Mind Crush; 2 x Divine Wrath
Side Out: 1 x Old Vindictive Magician; 1 x Gravekeeper's Guard; 1 x Crystal Seer; 1 x Creature Swap; 1 x Raigeki Break; 1 x Brain Control
Rug negates the effect activated on Normal Summon, Mind Crush uses the card revealed by Gadget, and Wrath covers effects outside that window. Keeps all six Main Deck LIGHT monsters to support both copies of Chaos Sorcerer.

Amazoness / Earth Aggro / Armed Dragon / Insect
Side In: 2 x Dark Renewal; 2 x Divine Wrath
Side Out: 1 x Old Vindictive Magician; 1 x Gravekeeper's Guard; 1 x Raigeki Break; 1 x Creature Swap
Renewal turns a small Spellcaster into removal plus a DARK Spellcaster, while Wrath prevents the monster engine from regaining tempo. None of the six LIGHT monsters for Chaos Sorcerer are cut.

Chaos / Zombie / HERO / Dragon Future / Red-Eyes
Side In: 2 x Kycoo the Ghost Destroyer; 1 x Cursed Seal of the Forbidden Spell
Side Out: 1 x Old Vindictive Magician; 1 x Raigeki Break; 1 x Smashing Ground
Kycoo prevents the opponent from banishing materials from the GYs without stopping your own Chaos plays; it does not block field materials. Save Cursed Seal for the repeated Spell that defines the opponent's engine during that Duel.

Gravekeeper / Harpie / Amazoness / floodgates
Side In: 2 x Dust Tornado; 1 x Cursed Seal of the Forbidden Spell
Side Out: 1 x Raigeki Break; 1 x Creature Swap; 1 x Old Vindictive Magician
Dust avoids paying a discard to remove Field Spells, while Cursed Seal punishes the repeated Spell once you have identified it.

Gravekeeper / Spellcaster / Wall Rock
Side In: 2 x Nobleman of Crossout
Side Out: 1 x Raigeki Break; 1 x Creature Swap
Three Noblemen including the Main Deck copy reduce the need to attack Spy, Apprentice, Crystal Seer or Set walls while keeping all six Main Deck LIGHT monsters for Chaos Sorcerer.

Make opposing attacks costly, protect the useful wall, and prepare a finish that does not depend on the opponent continuing to attack.

Game Plan
- Set an appropriate wall and keep Stronghold Guardian in hand to change a battle; do not reveal all your defensive options unnecessarily.
- Use Golem Sentry and Guardian Sphinx to return threats to the hand instead of waiting indefinitely for attacks into your DEF.
- Activate Weapon Change in advance and keep Gear Golem until your Standby Phase to turn its DEF into ATK and prepare direct damage.

Opening Turns
- A Set Giant Rat can access Stone Statue or Gear Golem when destroyed by battle; remember that the recruited monster arrives in Attack Position.
- A Set wall with Stronghold Guardian in hand and protection can punish the first attack; Des Lacooda must survive to produce draws through Flip Summons.

Key Plays and Synergies
- Stronghold Guardian sends itself from the hand during the Damage Step to give the attacked defender 1500 DEF; with Stone Statue, this increases potential counterattack damage.
- Cross Counter doubles battle damage when the defender's DEF exceeds the attacker's ATK, then destroys the attacker after damage calculation.
- Weapon Change only acts during your Standby Phase: pay 700 and swap the ATK/DEF of a face-up Warrior or Machine. Gear Golem can go from 800 ATK/2200 DEF to 2200 ATK.

- Weapon Change does not affect Stone Statue, which is a Rock, and does not swap stats immediately when you activate the Continuous Spell in the Main Phase.
- Guardian Sphinx requires a Flip Summon for its return effect; being flipped face-up by an attack does not trigger it.
- Staunch Defender needs your monster to be face-up; it cannot select a wall that is still Set. Waboku helps you survive but does not increase DEF or force the opponent to attack.
- Defense does not cover effect damage or removal that avoids battle. Keep an offensive route available, and do not treat this themed list as an automatic lock-based win.

title: Zombie
description:
Two Gozuki, two Goblin Zombie, and two Foolish Burial prepare the GY. Call of the Mummy puts large monsters into play from the hand, while Book of Life brings them back and removes an opposing monster.

NeoGoat Pro 0.3.2 beta.60 default deck | October 2026

PLAY GUIDE
Prepare useful revival targets, use Goblin Zombie's searches, and present large threats in successive waves.

Game Plan
- Use Gozuki or Foolish Burial to send a Zombie you can use soon: a boss for revival, or Gozuki to enable a Summon from the hand.
- Use Call of the Mummy before developing other monsters; your Normal Summon can then add Gozuki, Goblin Zombie, or an attacker.
- Save Book of Life to recover a relevant monster and banish an opposing piece; always keep the targets in both GYs in mind.

Opening Turns
- With Call of the Mummy and Ryu Kokki, Despair from the Dark, or Vampire Lord, summon from the hand first while your field is empty.
- Gozuki plus Book of Life can set up revival when the opponent already has a monster in the GY; if they do not, hold Book.

Key Plays and Synergies
- Goblin Zombie searches for a Zombie with 1200 DEF or less when sent from the field to the GY; Gozuki, another Goblin Zombie, Spirit Reaper, Des Lacooda, and Master Kyonshee are this list's options.
- Gozuki sent to the GY can banish another Zombie other than Gozuki to summon a Zombie from the hand; preserve that cost as well as the threat.
- Creature Swap can give away Goblin Zombie; if it later goes from the field to your GY, its search replaces a piece.
- Ryu Kokki punishes Warriors and Spellcasters after battling. When Vampire Lord deals battle damage, you declare Monster, Spell, or Trap and the opponent sends a card of that type from their Deck to the GY; it can also return after being destroyed by an opposing effect.

Common Mistakes
- There is no Pyramid Turtle in this Main Deck. Goblin Zombie can search for Gozuki with 800 DEF, but not Ryu Kokki with 2000 DEF or Vampire Lord with 1500 DEF.
- Call of the Mummy requires you to still control no monsters when its effect resolves; do not chain your own development that would invalidate this condition.
- Book of Life needs your Zombie and an opposing monster in their respective GYs to activate; having only your own target is not enough.
- Regenerating Mummy and Despair from the Dark respond to an opposing effect sending them from the hand; your own discards do not grant those benefits.

SIDE DECK GUIDE
Each plan starts from the original deck list and swaps an equal number of cards in and out. Choose a plan based on what you saw in Game 1; do not combine complete plans. These are practice guidelines with verified card counts and legality, not claims of proven performance in human matches.

Side Card Roles
- 2 x Tutan Mask: A dedicated Counter Trap that protects a face-up Zombie from Book of Moon, Ring, Enemy Controller, Compulsory and other single-target Spells/Traps.
- 1 x Deck Devastation Virus: Ryu Kokki, Vampire Lord and Despair can pay the cost. Destroys monsters with 1500 ATK or less seen on the field/in hand and on each draw until the end of the opponent's third turn after activation.
- 2 x Disappear: Chained to Call, Premature or Book of Life, banishes the key target from the opponent's GY without shutting down your own GY.
- 2 x Pulling the Rug: Negates Monarch, Gadget and Breaker Normal Summon effects when they resolve.
- 2 x Mask of Restrict: Shuts down opposing Tribute Summons while your large Zombies retain Book of Life, Call of the Mummy, Gozuki, Premature and Call as Special Summon routes.
- 2 x Dust Tornado: Removes Necrovalley, Royal Oppression and backrow that would block revival without negating your own Traps.
- 2 x Nobleman of Crossout: Removes Spy, Apprentice and walls without allowing their FLIP effects, opening attacks for Ryu Kokki or Vampire Lord.
- 2 x Divine Wrath: Negates monster effects, and discarding a Zombie helps Book of Life, Call, Premature or Gozuki's second effect.

Matchup Side Plans

Monarch / Gadget
Side In: 2 x Mask of Restrict; 2 x Pulling the Rug
Side Out: 1 x Creature Swap; 1 x Lightning Vortex; 1 x Des Lacooda; 1 x Morphing Jar
Zombie bosses still enter through Special Summons; Rug covers the summon that Mask does not negate by itself.

Zombie / Chaos / Red-Eyes / revival
Side In: 2 x Disappear; 2 x Dust Tornado
Side Out: 1 x Creature Swap; 1 x Des Lacooda; 1 x Morphing Jar; 1 x Smashing Ground
Disappear disrupts the target in the Chain, while Dust removes Necrovalley, Call, Premature or Continuous cards supporting the opponent's engine.

Book of Moon / Ring / targeted control and monster effects
Side In: 2 x Tutan Mask; 2 x Divine Wrath
Side Out: 1 x Creature Swap; 1 x Lightning Vortex; 1 x Des Lacooda; 1 x Morphing Jar
Tutan Mask only covers Spells/Traps that target exactly one Zombie; Wrath covers the monster-effect side that Tutan Mask cannot touch.

Gravekeeper / Spellcaster / Wall Rock / recruiters
Side In: 1 x Deck Devastation Virus; 2 x Nobleman of Crossout
Side Out: 1 x Des Lacooda; 1 x Morphing Jar; 1 x Creature Swap
Virus checks the field and hand on activation, then each drawn card until the end of the opponent's third turn; it does not continuously check cards added by searches. Nobleman removes Set pieces before their FLIP effects resolve.

Gravekeeper / Harpie / Amazoness / Field Spell backrow
Side In: 2 x Dust Tornado; 2 x Tutan Mask
Side Out: 1 x Creature Swap; 1 x Des Lacooda; 1 x Morphing Jar; 1 x Smashing Ground
Dust clears Necrovalley or the opposing Field Spell; Tutan Mask then protects a key Zombie from subsequent targeted interaction.
